 \gloproce@\( {e}_{j} \).))) 
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:e_j}
  {e}_{-1}=0,\ {e}_{1}={Q} -1.
 \end{equation}
A cell \( x \) is a \emph{colony endcell in direction \( j \)}\index{colony!endcell} 
if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Addr\/}}}}(x)\equiv {e}_{j} \pmod {Q}  \).
<!-- end definition-121 -->
<!-- condition-15: body_md -->
\label{cond:freeze}\index{condition@Condition!Freeze}
Only the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Freeze\/}}}} \) can change the field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}} \) (without killing
the cell).
<!-- end condition-15 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
It would be convenient here if our robust medium had range \( r>4 \), so cells
on both sides of the corruption can see each other.
But introducing ``action at a distance'' brings its own headaches.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- definition-122: body_md -->
We have a field called
 \begin{align*}
          \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} &\in\{0,1,\dots,\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\}.
 \end{align*}
Its default value is 0.
A cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}>0 \) will be called a \emph{healing cell}.
The field
 \begin{align*}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}\in\{0,1\}
 \end{align*}
will limit the healing process in time.
<!-- end definition-122 -->
<!-- condition-16: body_md -->
\label{cond:healing}
The rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}} \) is the only one changing the value of the field
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} \).
<!-- end condition-16 -->
<!-- condition-17: body_md -->
\label{cond:age-decrease}
The only rule in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \) field may decrease is \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \).
<!-- end condition-17 -->
<!-- example-23: body_md -->
\label{xpl:heal-sync}
The typical application of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) is, say, when in a domain of cells
with age values \( 1,1,1,2,3,4,5,5, \) the damage changes the values of three to 
 \begin{align*}
  1,1,1,0,7,6,5,5.
 \end{align*}
Now the cells with age values 0 and 7 become exposed towards each other, and
the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}} \) variable develops the values \( 4,3,2,1,-1,-2,-3,-4 \).
After this, \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) will gradually bring the ages closer to each
other.
Here is a possible synchronization history (time going downwards):
 \begin{align*}
 \begin{matrix}
      1&1&1&0&7&6&5&5
\\  1&1&0&0&6&6&5&5
\\  1&1&0&1&6&6&5&5
\\  1&1&0&1&5&6&5&5
\\  1&1&0&1&5&5&5&5
\\  1&1&0&1&4&5&5&5
\\  1&1&1&1&4&4&5&5
\\  1&1&1&2&3&4&5&5
 \end{matrix}.
 \end{align*}
As in the second line here, the synchronization
may not start in the best direction, but since the adaptation is towards
the fault in the middle, eventually the fault will disappear.

It is not hard to see that in general, if the domain to synchronize has width \( \Delta \) then
the synchronization will be finished within \( 2\Delta \) steps.
<!-- end example-23 -->
<!-- condition-18: body_md -->
\label{cond:anim,kill}
 \index{condition@Condition!Animation}
 \begin{cjenum}
 \item Only the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Die\/}}}}({p}) \) can kill a cell.
  It is invoked always with \( {p}\ge{p}_{1} \).  
\item
  \begin{sloppypar}
   Only the following rules can invoke \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Die\/}}}} \): \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Decay\/}}}} \). 
 \end{sloppypar}
 \item Only the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) can erase a cell (make it vacant).
  \item\label{cond:killing.protected}
A protected edge can be killed only if a neighbor sets \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Kind\/}}}}_{j}\ne\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Latent\/}}} \)
in its application of a growth rule or the end healing rule.

\item  Only the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Create\/}}}} \) can change \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j} \).
\item
  \begin{sloppypar}
Only the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) can create a non-latent cell,
invoked only by \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Germ-grow\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \)
(with the corresponding delay).
It is also the only rule by which a potential creator can arise in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:creator-emerging}.
      \end{sloppypar}
  \end{cjenum}
<!-- end condition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:exposing}\index{lemma@Lemma!Exposing}
  A rule exposes an edge only in the following cases:
 \begin{djenum}

  \item\label{i:lem.exposing.doom}
    Member cell whose neighbor is doomed, and dies at \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}=0 \), that is at a cut,
    as in Definition~\ref{def:cut}.

  \item\label{i:lem.exposing.channel}
   Channel cell, \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}=\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \).

  \item\label{i:lem.exposing.grow-end}
    Germ cell or growth, non-end-cell. \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}=\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}} \), or when
    a germ cell is killed by \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) invoked in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Germ-grow\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \).

 \end{djenum}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Direct consequence of the definition of siblings and exposed edges and
Conditions~\ref{cond:addr-age} (Address and Age), \ref{cond:anim,kill}
(Killing).
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:parent}\index{lemma@Lemma!Parent}
   Suppose that \( I_{1}(x) \) is damage-free during \( (u-T^{\bullet},u] \)
   (that is \( x \) is not affected via neighbors during this time,
   as in Definition~\ref{def:affecting}),
   and the non-germ cell \( x \) becomes animated at time \( u \).
   Then there is a \( j\in\{-1,1\} \) and \( t'\in(u-3T^{\bullet},u-{T_{\bullet}}/2] \) such that
the following holds:

  \begin{cjenum}

   \item\label{i:parent.gen}
\( x \) gets animated by
parent \( x+j{B}  \), whose state at that time makes it a sibling of \( (x,u) \).

\item\label{i:parent.sib}
If \( I_{0}(x)\cup I_{0}(x+j{B} ) \) remains damage-free during \( (u,u+T^{\bullet}] \) then
\( x \) and \( x+j{B}  \) remain siblings during that time.

\end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
We have an application of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Adapt}
from some \( y=x+j{B}  \).
So at the observation time \( t' \) corresponding to the switch
\( (x,u) \), we have the situation described by~\ref{i:parent.gen}.
To prove~\ref{i:parent.sib}:
according to Condition~\ref{cond:anim,kill}, the applied rule was
either \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal\/}}}} \) or \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}} \), creating a sibling with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \) equal
to that of the parent.
Dying can only happen by decay or purge, 
which takes time at least \( {p}_{0}{T_{\bullet}}\ge 2T^{\bullet} \).
The age of the child is made equal to the age of the mother.
In case of growth, the mother has time for at most change of age (with delay
\( {p}_{1} \)), and this will not break the sibling relation within time \( 2T^{\bullet} \).
The healing case is trickier since the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \)
in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Heal-sync} can also decrease \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \).
But given that \( x \) was just animated then if, say, it is created from the left, then
the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}} \) variables must point to the right.
Therefore the rule will not cause age change in the left neighbor as the ages are made
equal.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:glue}\index{lemma@Lemma!Glue}
Suppose that the adjacent cells \( x,x+{B}  \) are siblings just before the time
\( t_{0} \), at which \( x \) breaks the sibling relation.
Suppose also that both \( x \) and \( x+{B}  \) are unaffected by damage even via neighbors during
\( (t_{0}-T^{\bullet},t_{0}] \).
Then we have the following possibilities:
 \begin{djenum}

   \item A cut as in Definition~\ref{def:cut}.

   \item Cell \( x-{B}  \) was not a sibling of \( x \) at the last observation time of \( x \),
     and the switch kills \( x \) by \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Decay\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}} \) or \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \).

\end{djenum}
The statement also holds if we exchange left for right and \( x+{B}  \) for \( x-{B}  \).
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
f a cell \( x \) breaks a sibling relation by a rule, then one of the
cases listed in the statement of the lemma holds.
This follows from the definition of siblings, 
Conditions~\ref{cond:addr-age} (Address and Age), \ref{cond:anim,kill}, 
and the healing rule.
We will show that if neither of the possibilities listed in the statement of
the lemma holds then the cells remain siblings.
  
  \begin{step+}{step:glue.new}
  Suppose that \( x \) or \( x+{B}  \) were animated at some time in
  \( (t_{0}-T^{\bullet},t_{0}] \); without loss of generality, suppose that
  the cell was \( x+{B}  \).
   \end{step+}
  \begin{prooof}
  Then \( x+{B}  \) will be without an age change or dying for at least \( {p}_{0}{T_{\bullet}} \)
  time units which is longer than the whole period under consideration,
  as~\eqref{eq:p_{0}} implies \( {p}_{0} \ge 5\lambda \).
If \( x \) also underwent animation during this interval then the same
is true for it, hence the two cells remain siblings.
Suppose therefore that \( x \) has been live during \( (t_{0}-T^{\bullet},t_{0}] \).
The rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) implies that \( x+{B}  \) is not a germ unless \( x \) is
a parent.
If \( x \) is a parent of \( x+{B}  \), then part~\ref{i:parent.sib} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:parent} (Parent) implies
that the two cells remain siblings for at least \( T^{\bullet} \) time units; after
this, both cells have seen each other as siblings and therefore 
Condition~\ref{cond:addr-age} (Address and Age) shows that they remain siblings
until a cut or a death.

Suppose that \( x \) is not a parent of \( x+{B}  \).
If it has changed its age within the last \( 4T^{\bullet} \) time units, then it
will not change the age for a long time after, and the two cells remain
siblings.
If it has not changed its age within this time then for at least
\( 2T^{\bullet} \) time units before the observation time before the animation, it was
exposed to the right (since \( x+{B}  \) was latent), and therefore the rule~\ref{alg:Freeze} (\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Freeze\/}}}} \))
froze it, keeping \( x \) and \( x+{B}  \) siblings.
  \end{prooof}               

  \begin{step+}{step:glue.nonsib}
  Suppose now that both cells have been live during \( (t_{0}-T^{\bullet},t_{0}] \).
  \end{step+}
 \begin{prooof}
If \( x \) changed its age within this time, then it will not change its
age soon, and therefore remains a sibling.
Suppose therefore that \( x \) does not change its age during this time.
Suppose that \( x+{B}  \) became a sibling of \( x \) during this time.
Then it was not a sibling before, and the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Freeze\/}}}} \) rule must have frozen \( x \),
so \( x \) would not change its age so soon.
If \( x+{B}  \) was a sibling all the time during \( (t_{0}-T^{\bullet},t_{0}] \), 
then \( x \)
sees that \( x+{B}  \) is a sibling and will not break the sibling relation.
This is guaranteed even within the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \), which may change age
in both directions.
 \end{prooof}
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- definition-123: body_md -->
\label{def:links}
For times $t<u$, assume cell $x$ is live at $t$ and its body is
damage-free during $[t,u]$, and there are
no switching times in the open interval $(t,u)$.
Then we say that point $(x,t)$ is connected by a
 \emph{vertical link}\index{link} to point \index{link!vertical}
$(x,u)$.
If one end of a vertical link is not a switching time, then the link
is called \emph{short}. \index{link!vertical!short}
If cells $x,x+{B} $ are siblings at time $t$ or $(t-)$ such that 
$\left[x-{B} ,x+2{B} \right)$ is damage-free during $(t-T^{\bullet},t]$,
then the points $(x,t)$, $(x+{B} ,t)$ are said to be
connected by a \emph{horizontal link} \index{link!horizontal}.
                                                                
                                           
                                                                           
If point $(y,t')$ is, according to case~\ref{i:parent.gen} of 
Lemma~\ref{lem:parent} (Parent) a parent of point
$(x,u)$, we will say that $(y,t')$ is connected by a \emph{parental}
(maternal or paternal) link to point                       
$(x,u)$.
A \emph{link} is a link of one of these kinds.
A link is \emph{steep} or, equivalently, \emph{slow} if it is a non-short
vertical link or a                          
parental link.
(Since time is the second coordinate, steepness of a line is
synonymous to slowness of the  movement of a point along it.)
<!-- end definition-123 -->
<!-- definition-124: body_md -->
A sequence $(x_{0},t_{0})$, $\dots$, $(x_{n},t_{n})$ with $t_{i}\le t_{i+1}$
such that subsequent points are connected by links, is called a
\emph{path}.
                                                                        
                                                            
A path with only steep links is \emph{steep}, or \emph{slow}.
A \emph{backward path} is the reversed reading of a forward path,
backwards in time.
The adjective ``forward'' or ``backward'' will be omitted, when it is obvious from
the context.
For a path $P=(x_{0},t_{0}),\dots,(x_{n},t_{n})$ and
$t\in[t_{0},t_{n}]$, let 
 \gloprocpropo:cap@$P(t)$.))) 
 \[
  P(t)
 \]
 be $x_{i}$ for the smallest $i$ with $t\in[t_{i},t_{i+1}]$.
<!-- end definition-124 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:crossing}\index{lemma@Lemma!Crossing}
  Let $(x_{1},s_{1}),\dots,(x_{m},s_{m})$ and
$(y_{1},t_{1}),\dots,(y_{n},t_{n})$ be paths with $s_{1}=t_{1}$,
$s_{m}=t_{n}$, $x_{1}\le y_{1}$, $x_{m}\ge y_{n}$.
  Then there are $i,j$ such that $x_{i}=y_{j}$ and either
$t_{j}\in[s_{i},s_{i+1}]$ or $s_{i}\in[t_{j},t_{j+1}]$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let us call the point $(x_{i},s_{i})$ whose existence is asserted, the
\emph{crossing point}.
Let us replace parental links with horizontal and vertical connections as described
in the remark after Definition~\ref{def:links}.
Now the two paths cannot jump over each other.
Indeed, at the time of the crossing, the cells involved have to
be at a distance \( {B}  \).
At this crossing, one of the links must be horizontal;
suppose it is \( (x_{i},x_{i+1}) \).
Then either \( (x_{i+1},s_{i}) \) is on a vertical link between some \( t_{j} \) and \( t_{j+1} \)
or there is also some horizontal a link \( (y_{j},y_{j+1}) = (x_{i+1},x_{i}) \)
at time \( s_{i}=t_{j} \).
In both cases we can choose the crossing point \( x_{i+1}=y_{j} \) at time \( s_{i} \).
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-125: body_md -->
\label{def:traceable}
 A cell $(x,t)$ will be called \emph{traceable} if $I_{0}(x)$ is damage-free
during $(t-4\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}},t]$.
<!-- end definition-125 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:skirting}\index{lemma@Lemma!Skirting}
Let $\left[a_{0},a_{1}\right)\times(u_{0},u_{1}]$ 
denote the (only) island in the area under consideration.
Consider a traceable live point $(x_{0},t_{0})$.
There is a path going backwards from $(x_{0},t_{0})$ and ending
either in time $u_{0}$ or in a birth (in the sense of Rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Birth\/}}}} \) of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:Birth}).
It has at most $\Delta+1$ non-steep links (with \( \Delta \) as in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff})
which, with one possible exception,
form a series of up to $\Delta$ consecutive horizontal links,
and can only cross a colony boundary in the inward direction, and only if
$\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}<\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+\Delta$ on all cells involved.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
et us start constructing a steep path $c_{0},\dots,c_{n}$ with
 \[
  c_{i}=(x_{i},t_{i})
 \] 
  backwards in time from $(x_{0},t_{0})$, consisting of either vertical
links, or parental links if the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:parent} (Parent)
are applicable.
If we get to time $u_{0}$ then we are done.
Otherwise 
let us stop just before going below $u_{1}+T^{\bullet}$, with $c_{k}$ being the last element.
Then the body of $x_{k}$ intersects $\left[a_{0}-1.1 {B} ,a_{1}+1.1 {B} \right)$:
indeed, otherwise we could continue the path either by
a vertical or by a parental link.
The vertical link would be shorter than $T^{\bullet}$, and the parental
link would lead to a damage-free cell, so either of them would be
allowed. 

\begin{step+}{step:skirting.bridge}
There is an $i\le k$ such that
$(x_{i},t_{i})$ can be connected by horizontal
links that do not cross a colony boundary in the outward direction,
to a cell $y$ unaffected by the damage even via neighbors at any time (in the rectangle
under consideration).
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
Let us go back on the path for $k,k-1,\dots$ until the first
$i$ (counting from $k$) such that either $t_{i}>u_{1}+(\Delta+1)\tau_{0}$, or
$c_{i}$ is a parent of $c_{i-1}$; let us call it $i_{1}$.

Suppose first $t_{i_{1}}>u_{1}+(\Delta+1)\tau_{0}$.
Then there is some $i_{1}<i\le k$ such that 
$(x_{i},t_{i})$ can be connected by horizontal links to a directly
unaffected cell $y$. 
Indeed, if there is not, then $x_{i}=x_{k}$, $i=k,k-1,\dots,i_{1}$, since we have not
encountered a parent before.
The part of the domain containing $x_{k}$ that consists of cells directly affected by damage
has size $\le\Delta$.
If we cannot pass away from it via siblings within the same colony or towards the originating
colony then at least one end will be exposed and the depth will also be bounded by \( \Delta \).
This allows the $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}}$ rule to gradually eliminate this part, including $x_{k}$,
leading to a contradiction.
The time this takes is at most $\DgT^{\bullet}$ to propagate the depth
information, 
followed by $\Delta\tau_{0}$ to apply the steps of $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}}$ until $x_{k}$ is
reached, for a total time of $\Delta\tau_{0}+\DgT^{\bullet}$.
This shows $t_{0}\le u_{1}+(\Delta+1)\tau_{0}$ since \( \Delta<{p}_{0} \).
By the definition of \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \) this contradicts the assumption
of the traceability of  \( (x_{0},t_{0}) \).
If the only way to get by horizontal links to a directly
unaffected cell is to cross a colony boundary in the 
inward direction with $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}\ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+\Delta$ then
there is an exposed cell in the opposite direction, at distance
$\le\Delta {B} $, so $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}}$ will act again in the same way.

Suppose now that $c_{i_{1}}$ is a parent of $c_{i_{1}-1}$.
Let us then go back on the path for $i=i_{1},i_{1}-1,\dots$ until the first
$i$ (counting from $i_{1}$) such that $t_{i}>t_{i_{1}-1}+(\Delta+1)\tau_{0}$.
There is such an $i$, and we have $x_{i}=x_{i_{1}-1}$ for all $i$, since
the newborn $x_{i_{1}-1}$ cannot be a parent sooner.
Indeed, Condition~\ref{cond:anim,kill} says that animation happens only via 
healing or growth, and even the faster healing step has a delay of \( {p}_{1} \).
By the same reasoning as above, there is some $i_{1}<i\le k$ such that 
$(x_{i},t_{i})$ can be connected by a sequence of at most $\Delta$
horizontal links not crossing a colony boundary in the outward direction,
to a directly unaffected cell $y$.
\end{pproof}                       

\begin{step+}{step:skirting.finish}
There is a steep path backwards in time from the point $(y,t_{i})$ computed
above, going only either on vertical or parental links, and ending below time $u_{0}$. 
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
Let us construct such a path.
If it contains at most one parental link, then the body of cells it reaches
still is damage-free, hence the path can be continued.
On the other hand, it cannot contain two parental links, since
a newborn $x_{i_{1}-1}$ cannot be a parent soon.
\end{pproof}
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-126: body_md -->
A backward path is called a \emph{trace-back path} if every link in it is
chosen to be a vertical or a parental link if this is possible, 
with horizontal links only as needed in Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting).
<!-- end definition-126 -->
<!-- definition-127: body_md -->
\label{def:age-lag}
Let $P=\mathopen( c_{0},\dots,c_{n}\mathclose)$ be a forward path.
The \emph{age progress} of  $P$ is defined as
 \begin{align*}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{age-progress\/}}}(P) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{i+1})-\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{i}) \mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U} ).
 \end{align*}
<!-- end definition-127 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:trace-back-bounds}
  Suppose that a trace-back path $P$ with $n$ links 
has time projection $d<T_{\bullet}^{*}/4$.
Then the following holds.
\begin{cjenum}
 \item \label{i:trace-back-bounds.colonies} $P$ passes through at most 3
   colonies, for a total space projection of $<2.1{Q} {B} $.
 \item\label{i:trace-back-bounds.time} $d\ge (n-\Delta-1){T_{\bullet}}/2$. 
If the path has no parental links then the factor $1/2$ can be omitted.
 \item \label{i:trace-back-bounds.age} The age progress of $P$ is at most
   $n/{p}_{1}+\Delta+2$. 
\end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Let us show that $P$ can pass through at most 3 colonies.
It moves horizontally only along parental and horizontal links.
The latter only occur in connection with the application of 
Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting), with at most $\Delta$ horizontal links per
island. 
Given the time bound on the whole path, as long as it does not cross more than
three colonies, 
at most one island will appear, hence we do not have to count with more
than one series of $\le\Delta$ horizontal links.

Parental links can only occur in connection with healing and growth.
Healing moves the forward path towards the edge of a colony as shown
in rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Heal-passive}, 
only growth can move it towards the center.
In order to move towards the center of another colony, another growth cycle must
start (except in case of germ growth, which can span three colonies).
But definition~\eqref{eq:compute-start} implies that within the time bound
$T_{\bullet}^{*}/4$ the path cannot reach from the end of one growth to the beginning
time of another.

Let us prove the time projection lower bound.
There are at most $\Delta$ horizontal links and 1 non-steep link, 
arising from the island.
The other at least $n-\Delta-1$ links are steep.
A steep link is either vertical, in which case it has size
$\ge{T_{\bullet}}$, or parental, in which case it has size $\ge{T_{\bullet}}/2$.

Let us estimate now the age progress.
By the definition of the animations in healing and growth, age does not increase
along parental links.
Along horizontal links the age can increase by 1, and it can also increase immediately
after the last horizontal link.
It can also increase by 1 at the first link (in time).
But during the remaining vertical links, age increase occurs no
sooner than every ${p}_{1}$ steps, hence the total age increase is at most
$\Delta+2+n/{p}_{1}$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- definition-128: body_md -->
\label{def:gap}
Consider an open interval $G=(l,r)$ 
at some time $t$, where $0 < r - l$ is divisible by ${B} $.
                  
                                                                                 
                                                                                
                               
We say that $G$ is a \emph{right gap}\index{gap}
with \emph{size} $|G|=r-l-{B} $ if 
every traceable cell in $G$ can be space-consistent with $r$ only if it is a
germ cell. 
The \index{gap!right-age}\emph{right age} of the gap $G$ is
is the upper bound of the age of these germ cells (it is 0 if the gap contains
no germ cells).
If $G$ is contained in the colony of $r$ then it is called an \emph{interior gap}.
                                                                               
      
A \emph{right bad gap}\index{gap!bad} is a gap of right-age
\begin{align*}
  \lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}/2+1) 
                     
\end{align*}
containing an interior gap of size~$\ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}{B}$. 
If the gap itself is not interior then its right edge is required to be
an exposed right outer cell.
Left gaps are defined similarly.
<!-- end definition-128 -->
<!-- definition-129: body_md -->
Suppose that in a time interval $[v_{0},v_{1}]$, the gap
$G(t)=(l(t),r(t))$ is defined for all $t$, in such a way that all cells
$r(t)$ are space-consistent with each other, and $G(t_{1})\cap
G(t_{2})\ne\emptyset$ for all $t_{1}$, $t_{2}$ with $|t_{2}-t_{1}|\le 3T^{\bullet}$.
Then $G(t)$ is called a (right) \emph{gap path}, and the \emph{right age} of
the gap path is the maximum of the right ages of the gaps in it.
<!-- end definition-129 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
If a path space-consistent with $r(t)$ has the same
time projection $[v_{0},v_{1}]$ as the right gap path $G(t)$ and has no
germ cells younger than the right age of the gap path then it cannot cross
$G(t)$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:rn-gap}
Recall the definition of $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}$ in~\eqref{eq:gap-lb}.
Let $P_{1}=(x_{0},v_{0}),\dots,(x_{n},v_{n})$ be a trace-back path
(listed forwards),
let $L,k$ be positive integers with
 \begin{align*}
       L &< {Q} ^{2},
\\   k &< {U}  - 3 L{p}_{2}\lambda.
 \end{align*}
  Assume the following:
 \begin{cjenum}

  \item $y_{0}<x_{0}$ are in the same domain at time $v_{0}$.

  \item The interval $\left[y_{0}-2.1{B} ,x_{0}+3.1{B} \right)$ 
has been noise-free during $(v_{0}-T^{\bullet},v_{0}]$.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.gap-bds} $y_{0}$ is an exposed left edge at time $v_{0}$ (see 
Section~\ref{sec:edges}), and 
has been the right end of a  bad gap of right-age $k$
during $(v_{0}-T^{\bullet},v_{0}]$.
Its age is not within $\Delta$ steps of any of the age values listed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing),  with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.in-col}
If $y_{0}$ is a left outer cell then $P_{1}$ is in the same colony.
In this case, let $Z$ be the starting cell of the originating colony.
Otherwise, $Z=\infty$.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
  $v_{n}-v_{0}\le L\tau_{2}$.

  \end{cjenum}

  Then during $(v_{0},v_{n}]$, a right gap path $G(t)=(l(t),r(t))$ can be
defined, with $r(v_{0})=y_{0}$,
 \begin{align}\label{eq:gap-path.fast}
     r(v_{n}) &\ge  Z\land {\left( y_{0} + 
       {B} {\bigl(\mskip 1mu\frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{2}}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11\mskip 1mu\bigr)}\right)},
 \end{align}
\( \nonumber |G(t)| >0 \), with right-age $< k + 3 L\lambda{p}_{2}$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{crl:rn-gap}
  Assume the conditions of the Running Gap Lemma, further that
$(x_{n},v_{n})$ is not a germ cell younger than $k + 6L\lambda{p}_{2}$.
Then $v_{n}-v_{0} < \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
It is easy to see that the length of the path is at most $3L\lambda{p}_{2}$
(the proof is just like the proof of the lower bound on the length of path
$P_{2}$ in the proof of the Running Gap Lemma below).
Path $P_{1}$ starts to the right of the gap path $G(t)$.
Since age varies by at most 1 per link along a path                             
and since $(x_{n},v_{n})$ is not a germ cell younger than
$k+6L\lambda{p}_{2}$, no cell on $P_{1}$ is a germ cell younger than
$k+3L\lambda{p}_{2}$, while according to Lemma~\ref{lem:rn-gap}, all cells in
$G(t)$ space-consistent with $r(t)$ are germ cells with such age.
Therefore $P_{1}$ never crosses the gap path.
Inequality~\eqref{eq:gap-path.fast} gives a lower bound on how
fast $r(t)$ moves right.
                        
                                                                           
                                                                                
                      
According to Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds},
$P_{1}$ passes at most 3 colonies.
Edge $r(t)$ therefore can move right by at most $3 {Q} $, giving
 \begin{align*}
   3 {Q}  &\ge (r(v_{n})-y_{0})/{B}
\ge \frac{v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}}{3\tau_{2}}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11,
\\ v_{n}-v_{0} &\le 9\tau_{2}{Q}  + 3\tau_{2}(2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+11)+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} 
< 10\tau_{2}{Q},
 \end{align*}
 where we used~\eqref{eq:Q-req-1} and~\eqref{eq:destr-time}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
et $r(v_{0})=y_{0}$, and let $l(v_{0})$ be the leftmost cell such that
the gap $(l(v_{0}),r(v_{0}))$ has right-age $\le k$.
   \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward}
Let $t_{1}>v_{0}$.
Assume that for all $t\le t_{1}$, a gap path $G(t)$ is defined with the
desired properties and in such a way that $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ is not a germ
cell younger than $k+6L{p}_{2}\lambda$, and is traceable.
Then $r(t_{1})$ is an exposed edge, space-consistent with $r(v_{0})$.
    \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
    \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward.path}
Let us build a path.      
    \end{step+}
    \begin{prooof}
We start by building a backward trace-back path of length $m$
 \[
  P_{2}=((z_{0},w_{0})=(r(t_{1}),t_{1}),\dots,(z_{m},w_{m}))
 \]
ending at time $v_{0}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds} and the bound~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
gives
 \[
  m \le \Delta+1+2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}} \le \Delta+1+2L\tau_{2}/{T_{\bullet}} 
  <  3L\lambda{p}_{2}.           
 \]
The path does not end in a birth; indeed, otherwise $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ would be a germ
cell younger than $3L{p}_{1}\lambda$ contrary to the assumption.
It does not enter the gap; otherwise $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ would be a 
germ cell younger than $k+3L\lambda{p}_{2}+3L\lambda{p}_{2}$, which was excluded.
Therefore defining $x=P_{2}(v_{0})$ gives $x\ge y_{0}$.
Without loss of generality, we can suppose $x\le x_{0}$.
Otherwise, Lemma~\ref{lem:crossing} (Crossing) implies that path $P_{2}$
crosses $P_{1}$ and we can switch from $P_{2}$ to $P_{1}$ at the meeting
point.
Thus, $x$ is on the interval $[y_{0},x_{0}]$, aligned with $x_{0}$.

Combine $P_{2}$ and the horizontal path $H$ from $(x,v_{0})$ to
$(y_{0},v_{0})$ into a single chain of links.
It has at most $3{Q} $ horizontal links on $H$, 
and then at most $\Delta+1+2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}$
links on $P_{2}$, giving fewer than
 \[
   3{Q}  + 2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}} + \Delta+1
 \]
 links.
 We have $r(t)\ge {B}(y_{0}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11)$. 
                                                          
 Indeed, the only way for \( r(t) \) to move left is via an island (can happen at most once)
 that is then connected to the right end of the gap by healing.
    \end{prooof}

    \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward.exposed}
A protected left edge cannot occur on \( H+P_{2} \).      
    \end{step+}
    \begin{pproof}
      Suppose first that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a member or right outer cell,
      or a germ cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Addr\/}}}}>0 \).
Then the large bad gap on its left contains, by the definition of bad gaps,
a gap in the same colony or in the originating colony.
The path $P_{2}$ could cross it only by repeated parental links.
But the size of the gap is too large for using rule $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$, since the field $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}$
limits the number of applications.
Instead, $P_{2}$ (when traveled forward) would first have to walk right via
parental links to
participate in the creation of a colony and then walk back via parental links through the
expansion process from that colony---for which there is not enough time due 
to~\eqref{eq:compute-start}.     

Suppose now that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a left outer cell.
By requirement~\ref{i:rn-gap.in-col}, then the path $P_{1}$ stays in the
colony of $y_{0}$, and hence so does the whole gap path.
Since the cell is exposed, its age is already past the expansion stages.
Walking right, the age of cells on the path $H$ (which remains in the same colony
as well) does not decrease
except when it crosses into another work period (this is taken care of by our Definition~\ref{def:age-lag}
of age progress that uses \( {}\mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U} \)).
Indeed, by Definition~\ref{def:time-consistency} (Time consistency), the ages of siblings
must be non-increasing as one is moving away from the center of the originating colony.
It is also non-decreasing on the trace-back part $P_{2}$, except possibly on the 
$\le\Delta$ horizontal links allowed by that Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting).
Therefore the age of $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ cannot be smaller by more than
$\Delta$ than that of $(y_{0},v_{0})$.
If the age is not smaller at all then $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ is also exposed, since
the number of steps on the path is not sufficient to get into an expansion stage
of the next work period.
If decreasing the age by $\Delta$ makes it protected, then one of
the cases in Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing) must have occurred within the
last $\Delta$ steps before the age of $(y_{0},v_{0})$: but this has been
excluded by the condition~\ref{i:rn-gap.gap-bds} of the lemma we are proving.

Suppose that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a germ cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Addr\/}}}}<0 \).
                                                                   
                                                           
                                                                           
                                                                             
        
                                                                          
                                             
Since it is exposed to the left its age is \( \ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}} \),                       
and its address is \( >-{Q} \).
In this case, the same argument works as for left outer cells above.
    \end{pproof}
 \end{pproof}                     

A large gap cannot be closed by the healing rule, but it can be narrowed somewhat.
Suppose that for a gap $G=(l,r)$ the cells $r,r+{B} ,\dots,r+k{B} $ are siblings
with $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}(r+i{B} )=1$, $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(r+i{B} )=k-i$.
Then we set $r'=r+k{B}$.
If these conditions are not satisfied then set $r'=r$.
We define similarly, $l'=l-k{B}$ for an appropriate $k$.
The values $l',r'$ will be called the \emph{adjusted edges} of the gap,
and we will write $G'=(l',r')$.
the \emph{adjusted size} is $|G'|=r'-l'-{B} $.
 
 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.no-dam}   
Assume that the gap $G(t)$
with the desired properties was defined up to time $f_{0}$, with adjusted size
$|G'(f_{0})|\ge 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} {B} +2$ and right age $\le k$.
Assume also that in the area where we define the
path further, all cells are unaffected even via neighbors during
$(f_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}},f_{1}]$. 

Then the gap path $G(t)$ can be defined further in $(f_{0},f_{1}]$ in
such a way that as long as $r(t)$ did not reach $Z$:
 \begin{align}\label{eq:progress-right}
     (r(f_{1})-r(f_{0}))/{B}             &\ge
     \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{2}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-1,
\\\label{eq:progress-size}
       (|G(f_{1})|-|G(f_{0})|)/{B}  &\ge \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{3}} - 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} - 2.
 \end{align}
If $r(t)$ reaches $Z$ it never decreases again.
   \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
  Define $G(t)$ as follows.   
Suppose that it was defined up to time $t_{1}$, and let $t_{2}$ be the
next time that is a switching time of either $l(t_{1})+{B} $ or $r(t_{1})-{B} $ 
or $r(t)$.  
  We distinguish the following cases.
   \begin{djenum}

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $l(t_{1})+{B} $.
  If the switch is an animation creating a
sibling of $l(t_{1})$, then $l(t_{2})=l(t_{1})+{B} $.

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $r(t_{1})-{B} $.
  If the switch is an animation creating a
sibling of $r(t_{1})$, then $r(t_{2})=r(t_{1})-{B} $.

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $r(t)$.
  If $r(t_{1})$ dies, then $r(t_{2})$ is the closest cell to the right of
$r(t_{1})$ that is not a germ cell younger than $k+2(t_{2}-f_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}+1$.

    \item  In all other cases, we leave $G(t)$ unchanged.

    \end{djenum}

If $r(t)$ reaches $Z$, it will never decrease again.
Indeed, this happens only if left outer cells were exposed to the left.
Without loss of generality, assume that these outer cells were growth cells.
In this case, $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(Z)>\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$.  
                          
As $Z$ is protected to the left, the 
healing rule does not create a left neighbor of $Z$.
The only way that $r(t)=Z$ could move left is by the growth rule, but it
does not work for $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(Z)>\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$.

Let us show
 \begin{align}\label{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.spread}
       (r'(f_{1})-r'(f_{0}))/{B} &\ge {\left\lfloor \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{2}}\right\rfloor},
 \end{align}
which will prove~\eqref{eq:progress-right}.
Here we assume that $Z$ has not been reached.
Since the conditions of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.inward} are satisfied, 
the cell $y=r(t)$ is an exposed left edge for all $t\in(f_{0},f_{1}]$.
                                                    
                                                                             
Hence the longest it can take to move $r'(t)$ right is to
have the rule $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$ move $r(t)$ left by 
up to $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}$ cells; then all of them die by decaying.
The $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$ steps and the killing of the healing cells
take time at most $\tau_{0}$ each, for a total
of \( 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\tau_{0}=\tau_{2} \),
setting the field $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}$ takes time at most $\tau_{2}$, and the
final killing again time $\tau_{0}$.
                                                                         
                                                  
                 
                                                   
               

Now let us show~\eqref{eq:progress-size}.
The inequality
 \begin{align}\label{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.monot}
        (l'(f_{1})-l'(f_{0}))/{B}  &\le {\left\lceil \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}\right\rceil}
 \end{align}
follows from the fact that $l'(t)$ can only increase when
it is equal to $l(t)$ and increases via the the growth rule.
But the next application of $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}}$ is away by a waiting
period\index{period!wait} of length $\ge{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}$.
         

Let us combine~\eqref{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.monot} 
and~\eqref{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.spread}.
\begin{align*}
   (|G'(f_{1})|-|G'(f_{0})|)/{B}  
  &\ge (f_{1}-f_{0}){\left( \frac{1}{3{p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}-\frac{1}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}\right)} - 2.
    \end{align*}
Now, using the definition of \( {p}_{3} \) in~\eqref{eq:p_{3}},      
    \begin{align*}
\frac{1}{3{p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}-\frac{1}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}=\frac{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}-3 {p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}{3 {p}_{2} {p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}T^{\bullet}}
\ge \frac{{p}_{3}-3 {p}_{2}\lambda}{3 {p}_{2} {p}_{3}T^{\bullet}}
\ge \frac{1}{3{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}},
 \end{align*}
hence the estimate~\eqref{eq:progress-size}.
 \end{pproof}                     
 
 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.dam}
   Let $\left[a_{0},a_{1}\right)\times(u_{0},u_{1}]$ be an island with
   $u_{0}\in (v_{0},v_{n}]$.
Then the gap path $G(t)$ with the desired properties can be defined
for $t\in (u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}]$.
We will have
 \begin{align*}
        r(u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}) &\ge r(u_{0})-(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9){B} ,
\\ |G(u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}})|&\ge |G(u_{0})|-(2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+19){B} .
 \end{align*}
                                       
  \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof} 
Let us define $l(t)$ for $t\in(u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}]$.
If $a_{0}\le l(u_{0})+5.1{B} $,
then we set $l(t)$ to be the first site $x$ aligned with $l(u_{0})$
to the right of $a_{1}$ and $l(u_{0})+{B} $ that is unaffected even via neighbors.
This definition is justified, since growth or healing
do not have time to add any cell further to the right of $l(u_{0})+{B} $.
Now $l(t)\le l(u_{0})+(5.1+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+3.1){B} <l(u_{0})+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9{B} $.
                      
                 
                                                         
                                                      
                                                                                      
                                
                 
If $a_{0} > l(u_{0})+5.1{B} $, let $l(t)=l(u_{0})+{B} $ since, as noted above,
at most one cell can be added to $l(u_{0})$ by growth or healing during
$\left[u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}\right)$.
                      
                 
                                                          
                                                       
                                 
                 
The definition of $r(t)$ is done symmetrically similarly (but only as a lower
bound).
                       
                                               
                                                                           
                                                                                   
                                                                         
                                                         
                                                                           
                                                         

Thus, the island may decrease the gap by at most
$\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9{B} $ on one side; with another possible decrease of size ${B} $ on the
other side, this gives the size estimate of statement~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam}.
\end{pproof}                 

In the space-time rectangle considered, at most one island
occurs: 
indeed, \( v_{n}-v_{0}\leT_{\bullet}^{*}/2 \) follows from~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
and~\eqref{eq:compute-start}.
Use the construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} up to the time \( u_{0} \) of the
start of the island, then construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam}
from \( u_{0} \) to \( u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \) (or \( v_{n} \),
whichever comes first), then possibly again the 
construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} from \( u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \) to \( v_{n} \), we
defined \( G(t) \) for all \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \).

 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.age} For all \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \), the gap
\( G(t) \) has right-age \( \le k+2(t-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}+1 \).
In particular, according to the assumed bound on \( v_{n}-v_{0} \),
at time \( v_{n} \), it still has age at most
 \begin{align*}
   k+2(v_{n}-v_0)/{T_{\bullet}}+1 \le k+2L\tau_{2}/{T_{\bullet}}+1 < k+3L{p}_{2}\lambda,
 \end{align*}
as stated in the lemma.
 
    \end{step+}
   \begin{pproof} 
Let \( z_{1} \) be a live cell in \( G(t) \) space-consistent with \( r(t) \),
and let us build a sequence \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \), \( (z_{2},w_{2}) \), \( \dots \)
with \( f_{1}=w_{1}\ge w_{2}\ge\dotsm \) as follows.
Without loss of generality, assume that \( w_{1} \) is a switching time
of \( z_{1} \). 
If \( z_{1} \) is live at \( w_{1}- \) then \( z_{2}=z_{1} \) and \( w_{2} \) is the previous
switching time of \( z_{1} \).
Otherwise, either \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \) is a newborn germ cell, in which case the
sequence ends at \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \), or it has a parent \( (x,u) \).

If \( x\in G(u) \) then \( z_{2}=x \), \( w_{2}=u \).
Let us show that there is no other possibility.
Indeed, otherwise, \( z_{1} \) would have been 
created by animation which, by Condition~\ref{cond:anim,kill}
can only be by healing or growth.
Since \( r(t) \) is exposed, growth can only happen from the left.
We end up with one of the cases of the definition of \( G(t) \) above, and thus
with \( z_{1}\not\in G(w_{1}) \), contrary to the assumption.

By the parent construction, \( w_{2}\le w_{1}-{T_{\bullet}} \), and
 \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(z_{1},w_{1})\le\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(z_{2},w_{2})+1 \). 
The value \( w_{i} \) decreases at least \( {T_{\bullet}}/2 \)
in every step, while the age of \( (z_{i},w_{i}) \) can decrease by at most
1.
Since it can only end in a birth or a germ cell in \( G(t) \), this
and~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd} proves the age bound. 
\end{pproof}                         

\begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.finish}
Let us lower-bound the growth of \( G(t) \) for \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \).  
\end{step+}
\begin{prooof}
Since we applied the estimate of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} twice and the estimate
of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam} once, we get
 \begin{align*}
   (r(v_{n})-r(v_{0}))/{B}  &\ge \frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{2}}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11,
 \end{align*}
 and
\begin{align*}
    (|G(v_{n})|&-|G(v_{0})|)/{B}
\\                       &\ge \frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{3}}
     - 4\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} -2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-21.
 \end{align*}
 Hence using~\eqref{eq:gap-lb}, \( |G(t)| \) never decreases below
 \( |G(v_{0})|-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}{B} >0 \).
  \end{prooof}
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:healing-cause}
  Let \( c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0}) \) be a cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(c_{0})>0 \),
 \begin{alignat*}{3}
      D &= x_{0}+\left[-(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+0.1){B} ,(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+1.1) {B} \right),
\\   I  &= (t_{0}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}T^{\bullet},t_{0}].
 \end{alignat*}
Assume that \( D\times I \) is damage-free.
Then there is a backward path with at most \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-1 \) horizontal links,
at most 1 parental link, and at most \( 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} \) links altogether,
connecting \( c_{0} \) to an exposed cell.

A similar statement holds if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}}(c_{0})\ne 0 \), except that here the
length of the path is bounded by \( 2\Delta \), with \( \Delta \)
defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Let us build a path \( P=\mathopen( c_{0},c_{1},\dots,c_{n}\mathclose) \) 
with \( c_{i}=(x_{i},t_{i}) \) backwards with the property
that each of its cells \( c_{i} \) with \( i<n \) has \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}>0 \), and \( c_{n} \) is exposed.
According to Condition~\ref{cond:healing}, \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}} \) is the only 
rule changing the value of field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} \).
It sets the value to 0 immediately unless \( x_{i} \) is exposed or has a neighbor
\( c_{i+1} \) with a higher \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} \) value.
Therefore if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(c_{i})>0 \) and it was not set to 0 in the last step,
there are the following possibilities:
\begin{bullets}
  \item There is an exposed parent.
  \item The cell itself was exposed at the observation time.
  \item There was a neighbor \( y \) with a higher \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} \) value at the last observation
    time \( t'<t_{i} \) of \( x_{i} \).
\end{bullets}
In the first two cases, the path is finished with a last link.
In the last case, we add two links: a vertical link to \( c_{i+1}=(x_{i},t') \)
followed by a horizontal link to \( c_{i+2}=(y,t') \).
Since this leads to an increase of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}} \) value, the path can contain at
most \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} \) pairs of such links.

The statement on the field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}} \) is proved the same way, using
Condition~\ref{cond:freeze} and rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Freeze\/}}}} \).
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- definition-130: body_md -->
\label{def:boundary-path}
Let us call the sibling relation between two cells
\emph{strong}\index{sibling!strong},
if either they have been siblings for at least \( 2T^{\bullet} \) time units
or one cell is a parent of the other.

A cell is called for example a \emph{weak left exposed edge}\index{edge!exposed!weak}
if it is either a left exposed edge or
would be one in case it had no left sibling, and has no strong left sibling.
A sequence \( R_{1}=(y_{0},v_{0}),\dots, (y_{m},v_{m}) \) of cell-time pairs
with \( v_{0}<v_{1}<\dots<v_{m} \) will be called a \emph{left boundary path}\index{path!boundary}
if \( y_{i} \) is a weak left exposed edge during \( (v_{i},v_{i+1}) \) and one of the following is true:
      \begin{djenum}
        \item Cell \( y_{i-1}=y_{i}-{B}  \) dies at time \( t_{i} \) and is a strong sibling of
\( y_{i} \) at time \( t_{i}- \).
        \item Cell \( y_{i}=y_{i-1}-{B}  \) is created at time \( t_{i} \) by parent \( y_{i-1} \).
      \end{djenum}
<!-- end definition-130 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:bad-gap-opening}
 \index{lemma@Lemma!Bad Gap Opening}
 For \( m=\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \) let \( R_{1}= \) \( (y_{0},v_{0}) \), \( \dots \),
 \( (y_{m},v_{m}) \) be a left boundary
path that does not leave the colony of \( (y_{m},v_{m}) \) on the left
(it may leave on the right).
Assume that the the segment
 \begin{align*}
 \left[\textstyle\bigwedge_{i} y_{i} - 1.1{B} ,\textstyle\bigvee_{i} y_{i}+1.1{B} \right)
  \times(v_{0}-T^{\bullet},v_{m}]   
 \end{align*}
is noise-free.
Then \( y_{i} \) has at most \( {p}_{2}+{p}_{0} \) full dwell periods during
\( (v_{i},v_{i+1}] \), and there is a gap on the
left of \( R_{1}(v_{m}-) \) that contains a right bad gap.
The same statement holds if we interchange left and right.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Let us show that \( (y_{i},t) \) is a left exposed edge during
\( (v_{i}+2T^{\bullet},v_{i+1}-2T^{\bullet}) \).
Indeed, \( y_{i} \) can be a weak left exposed edge that is not a left exposed
edge only if it has a left sibling that is not strong.
Now, if \( y_{i} \) does not have a left sibling and it gets one then it
follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:glue} (Glue) (and the exclusion of cut, since the
it would not expose the edge) that the only way to lose this sibling is if
the sibling dies again, which it cannot do before making at least \( {p}_{0} \)
switches, becoming a strong sibling in the meantime.
From this, it is easy to see that \( y_{i} \) can have a left sibling
only during a time interval adjacent to either \( v_{i} \) or \( v_{i+1} \).
Since the sibling stays weak these time intervals must be at most
\( 2T^{\bullet} \) long. 

Now, as soon as \( y_{i} \) is a left exposed edge, unless the healing rule creates
a left sibling, it gets \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}\gets 1 \) in \( {p}_{2} \) dwell periods, and then the
decay rule kills it in further \( {p}_{0} \) dwell periods.
Hence within \( {p}_{2}+{p}_{0} \) dwell periods, the
boundary paths moves left or right.
Now a reasoning similar to part~\eqref{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.spread} of the
proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:rn-gap} (Running Gap) shows that the left movement is
associated with a healing step of rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}} \), and once the right
movement starts it will not stop before killing at least one cell with
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}=0 \).
Thus within each \( 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+1 \) moves, the edge moves right.
In \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}+1 \) repetitions of this, the weak left exposed edge moves right
by this many steps.
During this time, by~\eqref{eq:p_{2}},         
at most one growth step can occur on the left, so
a gap of width \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}{B}  \) will be created which is internal by definition, since we assumed that
the boundary path does not leave the colony of \( (y_{m},v_{m}) \) on the left.

To show that it is a bad gap, we bound the age of its germ cells.
The total number of (full or partial) dwell periods along the boundary path is
at most \( m({p}_{2}+{p}_{0}+1) \).
During this time, the age of any germ cell created in place of the killed cells
can grow by at most \(  \lambda m({p}_{2}+{p}_{0}+1)/{p}_{1} \).
By the definition of \( {p}_{i} \) in (\ref{eq:p_{0}}-\ref{eq:p_{2}}), we have
\begin{align*}
  ({p}_{2}+{p}_{0}+1)/{p}_{1} \le\frac{2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\lambda{p}_{0}+{p}_{0}+1}{4\lambda{p}_{0}}
  \le \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}/2 + 1,
\end{align*}
so the total germ age is at most \( \lambda \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}/2+1) \), making the gap
by Definition~\ref{def:gap} a bad gap.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:bad-gap-infr}
 \index{lemma@Lemma!Bad Gap Inference}
  Let \( c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0}) \) be a left exposed edge,
 \begin{align*}
    D &= \left[x_{0}-(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}+1.1){B} ,x_{0}+(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+1.1) {B} \right),
\\  I &= (t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{0}].
 \end{align*}
Assume \( D\times I \) is damage-free.
  Then one of the following holds:
  \begin{djenum}

  \item\label{i:bad-gap-infr.gap}
 There is a bad gap on the left of \( c_{0} \);

\item\label{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing}
  There is a boundary path of length \( <\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \) leading backwards in time from \( c_{0} \)
to a cell undergoing one of the changes listed in Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing}
(Exposing).

   \end{djenum}
  The same statement holds if we replace left with right.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
We will distinguish a special case when \( c_{0} \) is involved in the leftward rule
    \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{End-heal\/}}}} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:End-heal})
    case of healing, calling this the (leftward) \emph{end-heal} case.
    
    Let us construct a backward path \( (x_{i},t_{i}) \), \( i=0,1,\dots,n \)
    of elements of the colony of \( c_{0} \), made up of
horizontal and vertical links such that cell \( x_{i} \) is a weak left
exposed edge during every nonempty time interval \( (t_{i},t_{i-1}) \).
Suppose that \( (x_{i},t_{i}) \) has already been constructed.
  \begin{romanenum}

   \item
  If \( x_{i} \) has a switching time \( t' \) immediately before \( t_{i} \) such
that \( (x_{i},t) \) is a weak left exposed edge during \( [t',t_{i}] \) then
let \( (x_{i+1},t_{i+1})=(x_{i},t') \).

   \item
  Otherwise, let \( t' \) be the lower bound of times \( t \) such that
\( (x_{i},t) \) is a weak left exposed edge.
  If \( t'<t_{i} \) then let \( (x_{i+1},t_{i+1})=(x_{i},t') \).

   \item
If \( t'=t_{i} \) then at time \( t_{i} \), cell \( x_{i} \) became a weak left exposed edge without
switching, which can happen in the following ways::

\begin{varenum}{x}

\item Losing protected status via one of the cases of
  Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing), that is case~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing}
  of the present lemma.
  This cannot happen in the end-heal case.

\item By animation via a right parent, which by
  Condition~\ref{cond:anim,kill}, can only happen via the healing rule.
Let \( (x_{i+1},t_{i+1})=(x_{i}+{B} ,t_{i}) \).
Such an \( i \) will be called a \emph{right jump} (backwards in time).

\item Losing a strong left sibling by one of the ways listed in Lemma~\ref{lem:glue} (Glue).
It is easy to check that of these, only the death of a strong left
sibling produces an exposed edge in \( x_{i} \).
Each of the rules \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Decay\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Purge\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) that could have
killed \( x_{i}-{B}  \) presupposes that this cell did not have a left sibling at
the observation time \( t'' \) of \( x_{i}-{B}  \); thus, it did not have a strong left
sibling at time \( t_{i}- \).
On the other hand, as a strong left sibling of \( (x_{i},t_{i}-) \), it has
been alive for at least \( 2T^{\bullet} \) time units.
Let \( (x_{i+1},t_{i+1})=(x_{i}-{B} ,t_{i}) \).
Such an \( i \) will be called a \emph{left jump} (backwards in time).

\item\label{i:end-heal} The strong left sibling was killed by the right
  end-healing of member cells of another colony on the left (via \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \)).
  This clearly cannot happen in the end-heal case of the present proof.
  We will see, moreover, that it does not happen at all.
  \end{varenum}
 \end{romanenum}

  The construction can stop in the following ways:
  \begin{varenum}{s}
   \item The number of jumps on the path reaches \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \).
   \item\label{i:bad-gap-infr.neighb-col}
Cell \( (x_{n},t_{n}) \) would be a weak left exposed edge belonging to the left neighbor
colony.
This cannot happen in the end-heal case.
                                           
                                                                   
  \end{varenum}

By the construction, each jump is surrounded by vertical links.
For each left jump \( i \), cells \( x_{i} \) and \( x_{i+1} \) are strong siblings at
time \( t_{i}- \).
Let \( (x_{i_{k}},t_{i_{k}}) \) for \( i_{1}<\dots<i_{m-1} \) be the points
on the backward path with the property that to
\( (i_{k},i_{k}+1) \) belongs a horizontal link.
Let us number these points forwards in time:
\( (y_{0},v_{0})=(x_{n},t_{n}) \),
\( (y_{1},v_{1})=(x_{i_{m-1}},t_{i_{m-1}}) \), 
\( (y_{2},v_{2})=(x_{i_{m-2}},t_{i_{m-2}}) \), \( \dots \), 
\( (y_{m-1},v_{m-1})=(x_{i_{1}},t_{i_{1}}) \), 
\( (y_{m},v_{m})=(x_{0},t_{0}) \), 
creating a left boundary path as in Definition~\ref{def:boundary-path}.
If \( m\ge \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \) while we do not have case~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.neighb-col}
then Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-opening} (Bad
Gap Opening) implies a bad gap on the left of \( c_{0} \).
\begin{sloppypar}
In case~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.neighb-col}, the death of \( (x_{n},t_{n}) \) 
creates the weak left exposed cell \( (x_{n-1},t_{n-1}) \), a left colony endcell.
By Definition~\ref{def:edges}, this
is possible only by the shrinking process, as described after
Algorithm~\ref{alg:workperiod}.
(It is clear from there that \( (x_{n-1},t_{n-1}) \) is not a member cell.)
Continue the construction of the left boundary path.
Now it can be stopped in fewer than \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \) steps only by
one of the changes listed in Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing},
since \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}<{Q}  \); now Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-opening} is applicable.
  \end{sloppypar}

Let us now show that case~\ref{i:end-heal} does not occur at all.
Assume it does and let \( y \) be the right-exposed cell trying to do the end-healing.
Then we can apply the present lemma to \( y \).
Since it is the (rightward) end-heal case, a bad gap is implied on the right of \( y \),
so \( y \) is far on the left of \( x_{i} \) and cannot possibly kill its left sibling.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:cover}
Let $c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0})$ be a live cell belonging to colony $\mathcal{C}$ with
starting cell $z$,  
\begin{align*}
     I &=\left[z-({Q} +1.1){B} ,z+(2{Q} +1.1){B} \right).
\end{align*}
For \( J \) as in~\eqref{eq:J-K} let
\begin{align*}
n_{J}&=2|J|/p_{1}{T_{\bullet}}+3\Delta 
\end{align*}
 and assume that \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) does not intersect \( I\times J \).
Consider a trace-back path $P_{1}$ in $I\times J$ leading backwards from $c_{0}$
to a cell $c_{1}=(x_{1},t_{1})$.
The following holds.
\begin{cjenum}

\item\label{i:cover.stays}
  If $c_{0}$ is not an outer or germ cell younger than
$\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+n_{J}$ then the path $P_{1}$ does not leave its own colony.
  
\item\label{i:cover.xposed}
Assume $t_{1}\le t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}$, the rectangle
 \begin{align*}
    I \times(t_{1}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}]
 \end{align*}
 is damage-free, \( c_{1} \) is not a doomed member cell with  \( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{1}) > {U}-2{Q}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \).
Then the maximal domain containing the cell $c_{1}$  contains the colony of \( c_{0} \) as
 well as its originating colony.
                    
                                                                  
                              
                                         
                                                     
\end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
  \item\label{i:cover.age-incr}
    The age increase along the path is at most \( n_{J}\).
Indeed, for the path length \( n \) we have
$n\le 2|J|/{T_{\bullet}}+2\Delta+2$, from part \ref{i:trace-back-bounds.time}
of Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds} (where \( \Delta \) was defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}).
The age increase along the path can be upper-bounded 
using Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds} as
 \begin{align*}
     n/{p}_{1} +2\Delta+3 &\le 2|J|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} +2\Delta(1+1/{p}_{1})+3+2/p_{1}.
 \end{align*}
The sum all terms but the first can be bounded by \( 3\Delta \).

\item Let us prove~\ref{i:cover.stays}.
According to Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting), the horizontal links on the path
can only cross a colony boundary in the inward direction, and only if
$\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}<\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+\Delta$ on all cells involved. 
A parental link could be created only by the healing rule or one of the
expansion rules.
The healing rule does not act across colony boundaries, so
the later end of the
link along which the path is leaving would need to be an expansion or germ
cell.                           
The expansion rules do not work for cells past age $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$,
                        
so in each case, 
the cell at the crossing would need to have an age $\le\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$.
By part~\ref{i:cover.age-incr} above, the age could not grow beyond
\( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+2|J|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}}+3\Delta \), so it does not reach the lower
bound required by~\ref{i:cover.stays}.

\item Let us prove~\ref{i:cover.xposed}.
  Assume that the maximal domain contains an exposed edge \( e \).
Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference)
implies that either there is a bad gap next to $e$ or
we have case~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing} of that lemma. 

In case of a bad gap,
we can apply Corollary~\ref{crl:rn-gap} (Running Gap) to the assumption 
$t_{1}\le t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}$, where the role of the
path \( P_{1} \) there is played by path \( P_{1} \) here.
It implies that the bad gap cannot be inside the originating colony of \( c_{0} \),
nor can it be in the same colony (as the gap path cannot cross \( P_{1} \)).

In case~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing} of Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr}
there is a path of length $<\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}$ leading back to an edge that becomes exposed
by one of the cases listed in Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing).
If it is one the cases different from~\ref{i:lem.exposing.doom} then
it is outside the originating colony and pointing away from it.
Case~\ref{i:lem.exposing.doom} does not occur; indeed, it could only occur to member
cells \( c_{1} \), but the condition
\( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{1}) \mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U}|>2{Q}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \) implies \( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(e) \mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip{U}|>\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \).
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- definition-131: body_md -->
\label{def:attrib}
We  say that \( c_{0} \) is \emph{attributed}\index{attribution} to colony $\mathcal{C}$ if there is a path
$P_{1}$ going back to time $t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{attrib-t}}}}{Q}$, and a union $E_{0}$ of 
intervals of total length $< |K|/2$ such that $P_{1}(t)\in \mathcal{C}$ for $t$ in \( K \),
 and $\mathcal{C}$ is covered by a domain for all times in $K\setminus E_{0}$.
<!-- end definition-131 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:attrib}
Assume that the live cell $c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0})$ is traceable, and is not a
germ cell younger than $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+2|J|/p_{1}{T_{\bullet}}$.                              
Then we have:
  \begin{cjenum}

  \item\label{lem:attrib.expan}
  $c_{0}$ can be attributed to its originating colony.

\item\label{lem:attrib.no-expan}
  If it is a member cell, or an outer or germ cell older than $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}} + |J|/p_{1}{T_{\bullet}}$
  then it can also be attributed to its own colony.
   \end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Build a trace-back path $P_{1}$ from \( c_{0} \) backwards in time.
Due to the absence of  $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*}$, at most one island occurs in the area of \( P_{1} \).
Lemma~\ref{lem:cover} (Cover) implies that unless
$c_{0}$ is an outer or germ cell younger than $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}+2|J|/p_{1}{T_{\bullet}}$, we can continue
the path $P_{1}$ all the way to time $t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{attrib-t}}}}{Q}$ and stay in the colony
of $c_{0}$.
Let \( E \) be the set of times \( t \) of \( K \) that are either within distance \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} \)
of the damage or such that \( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(P_{1}(t)) \mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U}|\le 2{Q}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \).
Then \( |E|\le 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} + (4{Q}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}})\tau_{1}<|K|/2 \).
Lemma~\ref{lem:cover} implies that for all times \( t \) in \( K\setminus E \)
the cell \( P_{1}(t) \) is contained by a domain covering its originating colony.

In case~\ref{lem:attrib.no-expan}, the domain must contain the colony of \( c_{0} \),
because being past \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}} \) otherwise it would have an exposed edge.
So \( c_{0} \) can be attributed to its own colony.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:colony-trace-back}
Consider a time interval $(t_{0},t_{1}]$.
Suppose the following, with \( I=z_{0}+\left[-1.1{Q}{B} ,2.1{Q}{B} \right) \):
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rectangle \( I\times (t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{0}] \) is damage-free,
  and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) does not intersect \( I\times(t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{1}] \).
\item At time $t_{1}$, colony $\mathcal{C}$, with starting cell $z_{0}$,
is covered by a maximal domain with member cells in $\mathcal{C}$, and
no exposed edges.

\end{enumerate}
Assume that some trace-back path \( P \)
starts within $0.2{Q} {B} $ of the center at time $t_{1}$,
goes back to time $t_{0}$, and does not
come within \( 2 {Q}  \) steps of a work period boundary time.
Then:
\begin{cjenum}

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path}
Path \( P \) moves at most to a distance $2\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}{B}$ from where it started.
If there is no damage in \( I\times(t_{0},t_{1}] \) then \( P \) does not move
horizontally at all.

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover}
The colony $\mathcal{C}$ is covered by a maximal domain without exposed edges
also at time $t_{0}$.

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.progress}
    The age progress from $t_{0}$ to $t_{1}$ along path $P$ is at
most $\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}}{{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}}}+\Delta + 3$,
and at  least $\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-6{Q}$.
\end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{crl:progress}
  Under the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back}, suppose that
  the age progress along the path is \( n \).
  Then
  \begin{align*}
   (n-\Delta -3){p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} \le t_{1}-t_{0} \le 4(n+6{Q}){p}_{1}T^{\bullet}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
et $P=(c_{1},c_{2},\dots)$ be the trace-back path mentioned in the lemma,
  listed backwards  in time, with $c_{i}=(x_{i},u_{i})$.
In the given time interval, at most one island intersects colony $\mathcal{C}$.
Let \( K \) be the interval of times within \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} \) of 
this island, then \( |K|\le 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}T^{\bullet} \).
                                         

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.protected}
For times outside \( K \), 
the maximal domain containing the cell \( P(t) \) has only protected edges.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
If there was an exposed edge, then Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} 
(Bad Gap Inference), combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:rn-gap} (Running Gap) would
imply that the colony \( \mathcal{C} \) would not be covered by a domain at time \( t_{1} \).
\end{pproof}                                            

  
\begin{step+}{step:cover-trace-back.path}
Claims~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path} 
and~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover} are true.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The island may cause at most $\Delta$ horizontal links
(with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}), all other links are
vertical or parental.
As shown in part~\ref{step:colony-trace-back.progress.protected}, the
path can have parental links only within distance $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}$ in time of the island.
Since they use $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}}(\cdot)$ with a delay of at least ${p}_{1}$,
parental links are separated from each other by at least ${p}_{1}$ vertical
links.
If follows then, using the definition of \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \)
in~(\ref{eq:split-n}-\ref{eq:split-t}), that the path can move at most
\(    \Delta+|K|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} \) steps away, where
 \begin{align*}
   |K|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}}=(2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}})\tau_{2}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} \le 3\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}/2
\end{align*}
(and will therefore stay in the colony).
Assume now that, contrary to claim~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path},
there is a first cell $c_{i}$ with a parental
link to $c_{i-1}$, farther than $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}$ in time from the island.
Then $x_{i}$ is at distance at most $\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}{B}$ from $x_{1}$, and
as by assumption does not come within \( 2 {Q}  \) steps of a work period boundary time,
is an exposed member cell, or growth cell with age $\ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$, inside the the
colony. 
Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference)
implies then a bad gap which would not close until
time $t_{1}$, contrary to the assumptions.
Reference to the same lemma proves also the
statement~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover}. 
\end{pproof}                             

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress}
Claim~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.progress} is true.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  The upper bound follows because according to
  Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting)
  there are at most \( \Delta+1 \) horizontal links in the path, while
  along the vertical part of the path, age increases at most by 1 every \( {p}_{1} \) steps.
 We proceed to the lower bound.

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.path}
We will build a new path, \( P'=\mathopen( c'_{0},\dots,c'_{m}\mathclose) \) 
with \( c'_{i}=(x'_{i},t'_{i}) \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Start with \( c'_{0}=c_{0} \).
Within the set \( K \) we continue  \( P' \) as a trace-back path;
consider the cases \( t'_{i}\not\in K \).
We have \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(x'_{i})=0 \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}}(x'_{i})=0 \)
for times near \( t'_{i} \), since otherwise
Lemma~\ref{lem:healing-cause} (Healing Cause)
would imply the nearby presence of exposed edges.            
In the absence of freezing, the age cannot decrease in time.
If \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x'_{i}) \) did not increase in time \( t'_{i} \),
then this can only have the following reasons:
\begin{djenum}
  \item\label{i:delay.wait}
 Cell \( x'_{i} \) is in the process of decreasing its \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Wait\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{March\/}}}} \) variable
    from \( {p}_{1} \).
  \item\label{i:delay.parent} Cell \( c'_{i} \) has just been born.
  \item\label{i:delay.neighbor}
 There is a neighbor \( y \) at the last observation time \( t' \) of \( x'_{i} \) that does
 not let its age advance, by condition~\eqref{alg:March.sibling}
 of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{March\/}}}} \) rule~\ref{alg:March}.
 Thus it is either lower in age (call this a \emph{delay link of the first kind})
 or is equal in age but then it is closer to the center of the originating colony (call it a
 \emph{delay link of the second kind}).
\end{djenum}
In cases~\ref{i:delay.wait} and \ref{i:delay.parent}, let \( c'_{i+1} \) be
 found by regular trace-back: thus, the previous switching time of \( x'_{i} \) if
there is one, and the parent, if \( x'_{i} \) has just been born.
In case~\ref{i:delay.neighbor}, let \( c'_{i+1}=(x'_{i},t') \),
\( c_{i+2}=(y,t') \).
\end{prooofi}                                       

We will now lower-bound age decrease and upper-bound age decrease
backwards on path \( P' \).

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.inK}
Let us upper-bound age increase inside the set \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Inside the time set \( K \), the only horizontal links
on the path \( P' \) come from Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting),
adding at most \( \Delta \) to the total age increase backward.
There is no increase on parental links, and at most one backward increase on each
vertical link (as \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) may decrease age).
                                                                 
                                         
                                                                        
This is a total increase of at most \( |K|/{T_{\bullet}}+\Delta \).
\end{prooofi}                                      

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.nonK}
Let us lower-bound age decrease outside the set \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Going to the parent via
alternative~\ref{i:delay.parent} above is always going towards the
originating colony:
since we are in a maximal domain without exposed edges, the only possible kind
of cell creation is growth.
The cells created by growth have age equal to the creator cell.
During a colony work period, there are at most \( 4{Q}  \) growth steps (growing a
channel and then a growth arm to the left, and also to the right), this bounds the
number of parental links.
Let \( n_{1} \) be the number of delay links of the first kind and \( n_{2} \) that of
delay links of the second kind, \( n=n_{1}+n_{2} \).
We have
\(  n_{2}\le 2 {Q}  + n_{1} \), as one can move towards the center
of the originating colony only after being moved away from it.
The total age decrease on these non-vertical links is hence at least
\(  n_{1}\ge n/2 -  {Q}  \).
The total number of non-vertical links is \( m \le 4 {Q}  + n \), so
\begin{align}\label{eq:n1-lb}
  n_{1}\ge (m-4 {Q} )/2 - {Q}  = m/2 - 3 {Q} .
\end{align}
