In a vertical segment of the path of time projection \( l \),
age decreases at least by 1 in every \( {p}_{1} \) vertical steps.
So it decreases at least \( 0\lor(\frac{l}{{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-1) \).
Let us call a vertical segment \emph{short} if this number is \( <1 \),
that is whose length is \( \le 2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} \), else \emph{long}.
On a long segment of length \( l \), the decrease is at least
\( \frac{l}{{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-1 \ge \frac{l}{2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}} \).
Let \( L_{1} \) be the union of long vertical segments, and \( L_{2} \) that
of the short ones.
The time decrease on \( L_{1} \) is at least \( \ge |L_{1}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} \).
The number of non-vertical links is at least \( m\ge |L_{2}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -1\),
and by~\eqref{eq:n1-lb} the age decrease on these links is at least
\begin{align*}
   m/2 - 3 {Q}  \ge |L_{2}|/4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -3 {Q}  - 1.
 \end{align*}
So the total decrease of at least
\begin{align*}
  |L_{1}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} + |L_{2}|/4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -3 {Q}  - 1
  \ge \frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}- 3{Q}  - 1.
\end{align*}
\end{prooofi}                                       

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.sum}
Let us add up all the decreases inside and outside of \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
We get
 \begin{align*}
     &\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-3{Q} -1 - |K|/{T_{\bullet}}-\Delta =  \frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-V,
\\ V &\le 3{Q}  +|K|/{T_{\bullet}}+\Delta+1 \le 4 {Q} ,
 \end{align*}
where the last step follows from our assumptions about \( {Q}  \).           
At time \( t_{0} \), there is no exposed edge between 
\( P(t_{0}) \) and \( P'(t_{0}) \), since this would imply a bad gap between these cells.
This could not close, and at least one of the paths would need to cross
it in order to meet, which is not possible.           
Therefore these two nodes are connected by a chain of siblings and so
their age differs by at most \( 2{Q}  \).
Since \( P(t_{1})=P'(t_{1}) \), this shows that the age progress along \( P \) differs from that
of \( P' \) by at most \( 2{Q}  \).
\end{prooofi}                                      
\end{pproof}
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- definition-132: body_md -->
\label{def:successor}
Given a set \( E \) of cells at time \( t \), let us call a cell \( x' \) a
\emph{successor}\index{successor} of \( E \) at time \( t'>t \) if \( (x',t') \) is
reachable by a forward trace-back path of cells 
from some \( (x,t) \) with \( x \) in \( E \).
<!-- end definition-132 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:heal}\index{lemma@Lemma!Healing}
Let \( \left[a_{0},a_{1}\right)\times(u_{0},u_{1}] \) be an island. 
Let \( \mathcal{C} \) be a colony with starting cell \( z_{0} \), 
covered at time \( u_{0} \) by a        
domain of member cells, with no doomed cells of age \( >{U} -3{Q}  \).
Then a domain covers \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( w_{0}=u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-t}}}} \).
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
he damage affects directly at most \( \Delta \) neighbor cells of \( \mathcal{C} \)
   (with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}).
At time \( t \), let \( L(t) \) be the set of successors in \( \mathcal{C} \) of 
cells of \( \mathcal{C} \) on the left of the affected part, and \( R(t) \) the successors from
cells to the right.
(These sets are not necessarily disjoint.)
Both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) are (possibly empty) domains; indeed,
the only rule that would change the domain property is the killing
of a doomed cell at age 0, but there is not enough time for this. 
                                 
                                            
                                                   
                                                                                
                                                          
                                                                                         
                                                       

                                                               
                                                                             

\begin{step+}{step:heal.purge}
Let \( u_{2}=u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \).
If the sets \( L(u_{2}) \) and \( R(u_{2}) \) are both nonempty
then there is no live cell between them at time \( u_{2} \)
other than possibly germ cells with age \( \le 1 \).
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The only cells in question are the up to \( \Delta \) cells affected directly by the
damage, others could not have reborn yet after dying.
Consider the up to \( \Delta \) domains between \( L(u_{1}) \) and \( R(u_{1}) \);
they can shrink or merge during the time interval \( (u_{1},u_{2}] \).
According to Lemma~\ref{lem:short-exposed}, each will still have an exposed side,
hence each will be killed by the time \( u_{2} \) by
the purge rule (while having no time yet to grow due to the delay in the
rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \))---unless they are germs so new
that the purging did not have time to finish yet: in this case they have age \( \le 1 \).            
\end{pproof}             

\begin{step+}{step:heal.purge-end}
Any live cell at time \( u_{2} \) whose body intersects \( \mathcal{C} \) and that
does not belong to \( L(u_{2})\cup R(u_{2}) \) cannot be a member cell.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Assume by way of contradiction, that there is such a member cell \( x \).
  In this case clearly either \( L(u_{2}) \) or \( R(u_{2}) \) is empty; without
  loss of generality assume that \( L(u_{2}) \) is empty.
Consider a trace-back path from \( x \).
It cannot lead to \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( u_{0} \), since then according  to  part~\ref{step:heal.purge}
above, \( x \) would belong to either \( L(u_{2}) \) or \( R(u_{2}) \).
Therefore it must lead to a domain outside; given that \( R(u_{2}) \) is nonempty, this must be on the left.
Let \( y \) be the right end of this domain at time \( u_{0} \).
It must be outside \( \mathcal{C} \), so it is to the left of \( x \) whose body, by assumption, intersects \( \mathcal{C} \).
By Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting), the path has at most \( \Delta \) horizontal links,
and one parental link (there is no time for a complete animation delay),
so \( x \) and \( y \) are within distance \( (\Delta+1){B}  \) from each other.
All cells of the short chain from \( (x,u_{2}) \) to \( (y,u_{0}) \) 
have ages within a few steps of each other.
If \( (y,u_{0}) \) is a right colony end then \( x \)
(assumed to be a member cell to the left of \( R(u_{2}) \))
would have been purged away due to its small depth.
If it is not then the right edge of \( (y,u_{0}) \)  is exposed,
since it is either a member cell not at a colony end or a growth cell near the end
of the work period, and so during its shrinking phase.
But then Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference) 
would imply large gap on the right of \( (y,u_{0}) \), making the path from it
to \( (x,u_{2}) \) impossible.
(Indeed, due to the age of \( (y,u_{0}) \) the
conclusion~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing} of that lemma is not applicable.)
\end{pproof}                 

                                   
                                                                                        
                                       
             
                
                      
                                                                    
                                                                              
                                                                      
               
                                                                                      
                                                                                                   
                 
                                               
                                                          
                                                                                                 
                              

\begin{step+}{step:heal.size}
If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) survive until time \( u_{2} \), then
the gap between them will have size \( \le \Delta \) during the whole time.
If \( L(t) \) disappears then the 
the gap from \( z_{0} \) to \( R(t) \) has size \( \le 2\Delta \) during the whole time.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) survive, then there were up to \( \Delta \) cells
affected by damage between them.
Only these cells can disappear.
If \( L(t) \) disappears, this is only since its size was \( \le\Delta \) to begin with.
\end{pproof}           

 \begingroup\@ifundefined{if@tlamode}{}{\if@tlamode\tlachars\relax}\endgroup
\begin{step+}{step:heal.no-gap}If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) remain nonempty
then they will become part of a domain.\end{step+}
 \begin{pproof}
As shown above, between times \( u_{2} \) and \( w_{0}  \), the gap between
\( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) does not become larger than \( \Delta \).
Rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}} \) brings together \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) 
at some time \( t\le \Delta\tau_{1} \), at  some point \( x\in L(t) \), \( x+{B} \in R(t) \).
The possible germ cells of age \( <2 \) in the gap are not an obstacle: they
are weaker than the cells that are being created, so they will be erased.
It can only happen that \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) are not joined if
\( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x)-\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x+{B} )\mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U} |>1 \).
But as said in the remark at the end of Example~\ref{xpl:heal-sync},
then rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) will bring the two ages together
in time at most \( 2\Delta\tau_{0} \).           
This creates a single domain by time 
\( u_{2}+\Delta(\tau_{1}+2\tau_{0}) \). 
 \end{pproof}              

 \begingroup\@ifundefined{if@tlamode}{}{\if@tlamode\tlachars\relax}\endgroup
\begin{step+}{step:heal.fill}If \( L(t) \) does not survive then \( z_{0}\in R(w_{0}) \).\end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
The left endcell of \( R(t) \) will be exposed to the left and therefore the
rule~\ref{alg:End-heal} (\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{End-heal\/}}}} \)) will apply to it.
Part~\ref{step:heal.purge-end} above shows that no member cell's body intersects the
colony \( \mathcal{C} \).
Other possible cells that might intersect are weaker than the member cells that
end-healing creates,
and will therefore be killed off by rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Adapt}.
The end healing thus proceeds in time \( 2\Delta\tau_{1} \).
 \end{pproof}
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:mail-speed}
  Consider a case of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Post-mail\/}}}}(1,\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}},\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{G\/}}}},1,0,0,{Q}) \) when a track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}} \) is sent to a track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{G\/}}}} \)
  of a right neighbor colony (not necessarily adjacent).
  Assume that between the sending time \( t_{0} \) and the receiving time,
  the space-time area of concern is damage-free.
  For a cell \( x \) let \( d(x) \) be the distance of \( x \) from the right end of the
  receiving range.
                                                                                                  
                                                                                              
                                                                             
  Let \( x \) be a cell and \( y \) be a cell that is \( m \) steps
  (over neighbors) to the right of \( x \).
  Then at time \( t_{0}+2T^{\bullet}(m+2 d (x)) \) the information from \( x \) has reached \( y \).
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Induction on \( n= m+2 d(x) \).
  For \( i=0 \) the information did not have to travel any steps.
  So the statement holds for \( i=0 \) and hence also for \( n=0 \).
  Suppose that the statement holds for \( n-1 \), we will prove it for \( n \).

  Let \( y' \) be the left neighbor of \( y \), and let \( t'_{1} \) be its first switching time
  after \( t_{1}-2T^{\bullet} \).
  For \( y' \), distance \( m'=m-1 \), we have \( n'=m'+2 d(x) =n-1 \).
  By the inductive assumption on \( n \), information from \( x \)
  must have reached \( y' \) by the time \( t' _{1}\).
  It follows that at the decision time \( t_{1} \) of \( y \), it must have seen this information.

  If \( d(y)=0 \) then it has no right neighbor to consider and
  will receive the information of \( y' \) at time \( t_{1} \).
  Suppose that it has a right neighbor \( y'' \) to consider, and let \( t''_{1} \) be the
  first switching time of \( y'' \) after \( t_{1}-2T^{\bullet} \).
  Then \( y'' \) is at distance \( m''=m+1 \) to the right of \( x \).
  Let \( x'' \) be the right neighbor of \( x \), then \( d(x'') = d(x)-1 \),
  and for the pair \( x'',y'' \) we have \( n''=m''+2 d(x'') = n-1 \), therefore
  by time \( 2T^{\bullet}(n-1) = 2T^{\bullet} n -2T^{\bullet} \) the cell \( y'' \) has the information from \( x'' \).
  Cell \( y \) will see this and hence will be free to
  receive the information from \( y' \) at time \( t_{1} \) (if it still does not have it).
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- definition-133: body_md -->
\label{def:the-err-corr-code}
Our error-correcting code will distinguish, similarly to  
Examples~\ref{xmp:err-corr-code} and \ref{xmp:no-stretch}, information symbols
and error-check symbols.
A string $s$ of symbols that can be the argument of a
certain error-correcting decoding \emph{has $d$ errors}\index{error} if,
when applying the decoding and encoding to it, the result differs from $s$
in $d$ symbols.
We will work with a code 
\gloproca.greek@$\alpha$.))) 
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:err-corr-code-alpha}
  \alpha
 \end{equation}
of  Example~\ref{xmp:RS-code} that can
correct errors in $t$ symbols with just $2t$  error-check symbols.
When $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{loc\/}}}$ is a location representing a string $s$ then we will use the
notation
 \[
   \alpha^{*}(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{loc\/}}})=\alpha^{*}(s)
 \]
 for the value decoded from it.
 We expect having to deal with at most one  damage rectangle.
 It can corrupt a group of \( \Delta \)  
 consecutive cells (where \( \Delta \) was defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}).
The symbols of the code will be chosen in such a way that a code symbol 
stretches over $\Delta$ cells.
A damage rectangle can damage therefore up to 2 symbols, for which 4 error check
symbols suffice.
<!-- end definition-133 -->
<!-- definition-134: body_md -->
\label{def:packets}
  As the payload of a simulated cell is the aggregated payload of the cells
  of its simulated colony, we define the \emph{payload capacity} as
  \begin{align*}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Cap\/}}}'_{k}=|\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{k}|={B}_{k}|\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{1}|.
  \end{align*}
                 
                                                                                                   
                                                                   
                                                                    
                                                                                    
                                                                                                
                                                                             
We partition the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) field
into \( P \) sub-fields of relative width
\( w \) called \emph{field packets} numbered \( 0,1,\dots,P-1 \).
The \( i \)th field packet of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) field will be denoted \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{i} \).
We also partition each track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}} \) of whole colony into \( P^{*} \) \emph{track packets}
of \( w^{*}{Q}  \) cells each.
The \( j \)th track packet, with addresses in \( \left[jw^{*}{Q},(j+1)w^{*}{Q}\right) \),
will be denoted as the \emph{location} \( \_\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}_{j} \),
In particular the \( j \)th track packet of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) track is location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \)
<!-- end definition-134 -->
<!-- definition-135: body_md -->
\label{def:PlRedun}
The error checks of track packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \), will be in location
  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \) on the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Pl-redun\/}}}} \) track.
Location 
\begin{align}\label{eq:lPayload'}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{j}=\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j}\cup\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j}
\end{align}
combines location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) with its error check symbols for a complete code.

We consider the whole \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) track
of each consecutive \( \Delta \) cells in the packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) as an
information symbol; the error check symbols of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) go to
location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \).
To avoid that the damage rectangle affect both an information symbol and an error-check symbol
of the same code, we divide the track packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{j} \) into left and right halves.
The error checks for the left half of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) go into the right half of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \),
and those for the right half go into the left half of the same.
<!-- end definition-135 -->
<!-- definition-136: body_md -->
\label{def:encoding}
The encoding 
 \begin{align*}
  \varphi_{*}:{\mathbb{S}}_{k+1}\to{\mathbb{S}}_{k}^{{Q} _{k}}
 \end{align*}
takes the state of a cell, applies to it the 
error-correcting code $\alpha_{*}$ introduced above in
Definition~\ref{def:the-err-corr-code} and
copies the result to the $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Info\/}}}}$ track of a colony.
The other parts of the colony are set in such a way as they are to be
found at the beginning of a work period.
<!-- end definition-136 -->
<!-- definition-137: body_md -->
\label{def:decoding}
If the \( (x,t) \) is not in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \), then define
 \[
 \eta^{*}(x,t)=\varphi^{*}(x,t)=\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Vac\/}}},
 \]
 unless there is a latest time \( t'\in (t-2{Q} T^{\bullet},t] \) that is a switching time
of a cell of \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) such that the rectangle
\begin{align*}
 \left[x-({Q} +1.1){B} ,x+(2{Q} +1.1{B} )\right)\times(t'-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t']  
\end{align*}
is damage-free, and the colony is covered by a domain of 
cells belonging to the same work period
(the condition on switching just makes sure that a ``latest'' value exists).
In the latter case, let us define the 
strings \( s=\eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t').\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Util\/}}}} \) and \( p_{i}=\eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t').\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{i} \).
For the decoded value to be nonvacant, we also require that each of \( s,p_{i} \)
contains at most 4 errors in the sense that \( \alpha_{*}(\alpha^{*}(s)) \) differs
from \( s \) in at most 4 places of up to 2 consecutive symbols) and the same for each \( p_{i} \)
for \( i=0,\dots,P^{*}-1 \).
              
If this is satisfied, then \( \eta^{*}(x,t).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}^{c}=\alpha^{*}(s) \) while
\( \eta^{*}(x,t).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) is the concatenation of all \( \alpha^{*}(p_{i}) \).
We will say that \( \eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t) \) is \emph{error-free} if each of \( s,p_{i} \) are error-free.
<!-- end definition-137 -->

<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:legalize}
  After an application of the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Legalize\/}}}}(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I)) \), location
  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) contains a word with at most 2 errors.
  Moreover, if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) has at most 2 errors and decodes to some value \( X \)
  then result also decodes to \( X \).
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Suppose first that \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) has at most \( 2 \) errors and decodes to \( X \).
Consider any one of the two repetitions;
the decoding-encoding writes \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Vote\/}}}}_{j}(I) \).
If damage happens during it then the result is worthless.
But otherwise, earlier damage could add at most 2 more errors,
and since \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Decode\/}}}} \) corrects 4 errors, the result in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Vote\/}}}}_{j} \)
is the code of \( X \).
Therefore the result in the first repetition differs from the code of \( X \) in
the at most 2 errors added possibly in the last majority step.
The same reasoning applies to the second repetition.

Suppose now that \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) is an arbitrary word.
Suppose that damage does not occur in the first repetition.
Then this part turns \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) into a code word (without errors),
and the previous analysis applies to the second repetition.
If damage occurs in the first repetition then
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \) may be again arbitrary as the result of this part.
But then the second repetition is damage-free and writes a code word
into \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}(I) \).
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:free-past}
For some time \( t \), let \( J=(t-2T^{\bullet *}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t] \).
Assume that the rectangle \( I\times J \) is damage-free, and at time \( t \)
the colony \( \mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}(x) \) is covered by a domain of cells belonging to the same work period.
Then the string \( \eta(\mathcal{C},t) \) is error-free in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:decoding}.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Suppose that during the whole interval \( (t-2T^{\bullet *},t] \), the colony \( \mathcal{C} \)
is covered by a domain.
In the absence of damage, this colony performs at least one complete work period
of computation without any interference from errors inside \( \mathcal{C} \).
It follows then from the definition of the program (summarized in Algorithm~\ref{alg:workperiod})
that the string \( s \), as a result of such a computation, is error-free.

Suppose now that there is a first time \( t'>t-2T^{\bullet *} \) such that the colony
is covered by a domain after \( t' \), but not before.
Leading back a trace-back path from any cell of \( \mathcal{C} \), starting at time \( t' \)
the path is at any time in a domain covering its originating colony.
Indeed, otherwise Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference) implies
a bad gap which would not be closed, contradicting the assumption that \( \mathcal{C} \)
is covered by a domain at time \( t \).
The only possibility is thus that of a growing arm that finishes covering \( \mathcal{C} \) at
time \( t' \).

Now if \( t'\le t-1.5T^{\bullet *} \) Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back} (Colony Trace-back)
together with the number of steps allowed between the end of growth and the
work period end
implies that a new work period starts before time \( t-T^{\bullet *} \),
leaving a whole work period until time, guaranteeing an error-free colony.
If \( t'> t-1.5T^{\bullet *} \) then Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back}
together with the number of steps allowed between the start and end of growth
implies that the growth started after time \( t-2T^{\bullet *} \)
using the growth rule, so by the time \( t' \) the whole colony 
encodes a latent big cell in an error-free way.
No new errors arise later.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:legality}
  Assume that, for some number \( a \), the set \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) does not
intersect \( \left[x,x+{Q} {B} \right)\times(a-2T^{\bullet *},a+2T^{\bullet *}] \), 
             
further that \( \sigma_{1},\sigma_{2} \),
as in Definition~\ref{def:special-sw-times} (Special switching times)
are defined for cell \( x \) of medium \( M^{*} \) in the interval \( (a-2T^{\bullet *},a+2T^{\bullet *}] \),
using Definition~\ref{def:decoding} (Decoding).
Then the following holds, using Definition~\ref{def:legal} (Legality):
\begin{cjenum}
  \item\label{i:legality.legal}
    \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{legal\/}}}_{k+1}(\eta^{*}(x, \sigma_{2}-), \eta^{*}(x, \sigma_{2})) = 1 \), thus
    proving Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.legal-comp}.
  \item\label{i:legality.time-bounds}
    \( T_{\bullet}^{*} \le \sigma_{2} - \sigma_{1} \le T^{\bullet *} \), thus proving
    Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.dwell-pd-bd}.

    \begin{sloppypar}
\item\label{i:legality.rand} The randomization property
  \( g(\alpha(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{rand\/}}}),j, W_{0}(x,a),\eta^{*}) \), as defined
  in Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.rand}
  will hold: it can be expressed in the needed canonical simulation of
  Definition~\ref{def:canon-simul}.      
    \end{sloppypar}
\end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
et \( I=\left[x,x+{Q}  {B} \right) \).
Our assumption implies that damage is covered by at most one island in 
\( I\times(a-2T^{\bullet *},a+2T^{\bullet *}] \).
             
According to Definition~\ref{def:decoding} (Decoding), there is a latest time \( v_{2} \) 
in \( (\sigma_{2}-2{Q}T^{\bullet},\sigma_{2}] \) that is a switching time
of a cell of colony \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) such that \( I \) is damage-free during
\( (v_{2}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},v_{2}] \), and at time \( v_{2} \) the colony
is covered by a domain of cells belonging to the same work period.
The value \( \eta^{*}(x,\sigma_{2}) \) was decoded from the state of the colony at
time \( v_{2} \).
Let \( y_{1} \) be the cell with address \( {\lfloor {Q} /2\rfloor} \) in colony
\( \mathcal{C}(x) \), then \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) is traceable, as in
Definition~\ref{def:traceable}.
Build a trace-back path from \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) 
to the latest time \( v_{1} \) in
\( (\sigma_{1}-2{Q}T^{\bullet},\sigma_{1}] \) at which the colony is again covered with
member cells belonging to the same work period,
moreover \( I \) is damage-free during \( (v_{1}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},v_{1}] \). 
There is such a time, due to the definition of \( \sigma_{1} \).
                                                                                     
Since \( \sigma_{1},\sigma_{2} \) are defined, 
the colony \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) encodes at time \( v_{1} \) with at
most 4 errors a big cell with value different from the one
encoded at time \( v_{2} \).

\begin{step+}{step:legality.free}
If \( I \) is damage-free during \( (v_{1},v_{2}] \) then
claim~\ref{i:legality.legal} holds.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The computation runs now without faults, and as planned, computes an error-free
value.
Rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \) in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Compute} applies \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Legalize\/}}}} \) to
the information retrieved from the neighbor colonies, so the result
computed from this information will be a legal one.
The switching time \( \sigma_{2} \) occurs just when the last cell of the colony
passes to a new work period. 
The process makes sure that either all cells of the colony are doomed (when the
computed value is vacant), or none them.
If they are doomed then the whole colony dies.
Otherwise, the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Finish\/}}}} \) installs the remaining changes in one step.
In both cases, the state at time \( \sigma_{2} \) will be a legal consequence of
the state at time \( \sigma_{2}- \).
\end{pproof}                     

\begin{step+}{step:legality.non-free}
If \( I \) is not damage-free during \( (v_{1},v_{2}] \) then 
claim~\ref{i:legality.legal} still holds.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
Let \( t_{1}\in(v_{1},v_{2}] \) be some time at which damage intersects \( I \),
and let \( t_{0} \) be the latest time before \( \min(t_{1}-1.1\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}, v_{1}) \) which is the
switching time of some cell, with the
property that all cells of the colony belong to the same work period.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cover} (Cover), at time \( t_{0} \), the colony is covered by a
domain of cells.
Lemma~\ref{lem:free-past} implies that the colony encodes an error-free string.

Let us follow the development of the colony forward in time, 
starting from \( t_{0} \).
Healing succeeds, due to the Cover Lemma.
Locally maintained fields will be restored in a short time following the
occurrence of damage, via the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Loc-maintain\/}}}} \) while other fields
changed in at most an interval of \( \Delta \) cells, with \( \Delta \)
defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.
After this, the work of the colony can be followed as before.

The time of the damage may fall into at most one of the three iterations of
any of the rules with three iterations (\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Refresh-payload\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-payload\/}}}} \),
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Legalize\/}}}} \),  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \)).
The output of this one iteration in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Vote\/}}}}_{r} \)
will be outvoted by the other two values in the final majority vote.
                                                                                          
                                                 
So the only errors in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Hold\/}}}} \) can be the ones due
to their short-term damage in the final majority vote; 
these change at most \( \Delta \) cells.
In summary, we can make the same conclusion as
part~\ref{step:legality.free}, except that the encoded string may contain up to
2 errors (in case the island occurs in the last part of computation or later).

There is an exception to this reasoning: in the rules \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Refresh-payload\/}}}} \) and
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-payload\/}}}} \), the copy command is not repeated three times, so
it is protected from the damage only in a limited
way in the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Move-mail\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:move-mail-2}.
This protection makes sure that wrong information planted by damage 
is copied to at most one segment of size \( \Delta \); however, that one segment
will still be affected, so the damage rectangle can cause 2 errors in the place it occurs and 2
more in the place to which the information is carried.
But the error-correcting code, being able to correct 4 errors, will still deal with this.
\end{pproof}                         

\begin{step+}{step:legality.time-lb}
We have \( T_{\bullet}^{*} \le \sigma_{2} - \sigma_{1} \).
 \end{step+}
 \begin{pproof}
Consider a cell \( y \) of the colony,
for example the one with address \( {\lfloor {Q} /2\rfloor} \), and lead a trace-back path from
time \( \sigma_{2} \) to time \( \sigma_{1} \).
Suppose it has \( n \) links: none of these are parental.
At time \( \sigma_{j}- \) all cells have ages \( \ge {U} -2{Q}  \),          
hence the age progress along the path is at least \( {U} -2{Q}  \).

By Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds}, the age progress is 
\( {U} -2{Q} \le n/{p}_{1}+\Delta+2 \), hence 
 \begin{align*}
   n\ge {p}_{1}{U} -{p}_{1}(2{Q} +\Delta+2).
 \end{align*}
By the same lemma, 
 \begin{align*}
\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{1} &\ge n{T_{\bullet}}-(\Delta+1){T_{\bullet}} 
\\ &\ge {T_{\bullet}}{\left( {p}_{1}{U}  -{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}\right)}
\\ &=  {T_{\bullet}}{U}' -{T_{\bullet}}{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}
   \\ &=  {T_{\bullet}}{U}'{\left( 1-{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}/{U}'\right)}
\\ &\ge{T_{\bullet}}{U}' (1-R{Q}/{U}') = {T_{\bullet}}^{*},
 \end{align*}
 where we used~\eqref{eq:U-def}, further
 \( {U}'={U}'_{k} \) was defined in Section~\ref{sec:amp}.
Indeed, sufficiently large \( R \) will satisfy the last inequality.
\end{pproof}                       

\begin{step+}{step:legality.time-ub}
We have \( \sigma_{2} - \sigma_{1}\leT^{\bullet *} \).
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back} (Colony Trace-back) lower-bounds
the progress along a trace-back path;
then the proof is finished similarly to part~\ref{step:legality.time-lb} above.
\end{pproof}                        
\begin{step+}{step:legality.rand}
 Let us prove~\ref{i:legality.rand}. 
\end{step+}
\begin{prooof}
  We need to prove essentially \( \operatorname{\mathsf P}\mathopen\{\mskip 1mu\eta^{*}(x,\sigma_{2}).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Rand\/}}}}=j\mskip 1mu\mathclose\}\le 1/2+eps'+\varepsilon'' \),
  given how \( \varepsilon'_{k} \) is defined in~\eqref{eq:eps-defs}.
  Here \( \varepsilon'' \) bounds the probability that damage occurs in the window \( W_{0}(x,a) \) at all.
  On the other hand, when it does not occur then each cell at each time within the work period
  performs its needed action: in particular, it carries out the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \) of
  Algorithm~\ref{alg:Compute}, and within it, the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Randomize\/}}}} \).
  This rule relies on the randomization action of a well-defined cell at a well-defined age
  of the work period, with the result being \( j \) with probability \( \le 1/2+\varepsilon' \).
  The probability can only be increased by the probability bound that damage does occur in \( W_{0} \).
  It would be now just a tedious exercise to actually express \( g(\alpha(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{rand\/}}}),j, W_{0}(x,a),\eta^{*}) \)
  formally as needed by a canonical simulation.
\end{prooof}
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
Assuming \( \eta \) is a trajectory, \( \eta^{*} \) satisfies
  Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.legal-birth}.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
The proof is similar to that of the above lemma, only simpler.
There is a latest time \( v_{2} \) 
in \( (\sigma_{2}-2{Q}T^{\bullet},\sigma_{2}] \) that is a switching time
of a cell of colony \( \mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}(x) \) such that \( I \) is damage-free during
\( (v_{2}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},v_{2}] \), and at time \( v_{2} \) the colony
is covered by a domain of cells belonging to the same work period.
The value \( \eta^{*}(x,\sigma_{2}) \) was decoded from the state of the colony at
time \( v_{2} \).
Let \( y_{1} \) be the cell with address \( {\lfloor {Q} /2\rfloor} \) in colony
\( \mathcal{C}(x) \), then \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) is traceable, as in
Definition~\ref{def:traceable}.
Now the a trace-back path from \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) will lead to a
cell still near the middle of colony \( \mathcal{C} \), where \( \mathcal{C} \) is now not covered
by member cells.
According to the Cover Lemma it the cell is still in a domain without exposed edges,
so this domain will cover \( \mathcal{C} \) as well as an originating colony.
Tracing back further one can see that the cells covering \( \mathcal{C} \) (whether outer or germ)
were all formed by the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \) or \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Germ-grow\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{passive\/}}}} \)
of Algorithms~\ref{alg:Grow.passive}, \ref{alg:Germ-grow.passive}
so they encode a latent big cell.
This is in accordance with Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.legal-birth}, as the
rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Birth\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Birth} requires that a cell born from a vacant one is latent.
The trace-back also shows that the germ growth succeeded only if the created colony
is at a distance \( \ge 2{Q}{B} \) from existing big cells, as requires the definition of emergence.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:update-loc-maint}
Under the same condition on \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) as in Lemma~ \ref{lem:legality},
  assume that we have a full colony in which all cells have ages before
  the start of rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-loc-maint\/}}}} \) (Algorithm~\ref{alg:Update-loc-maint}).

 \begin{cjenum}

 \item\label{i:update-loc-maint.damage}
The locally maintained fields \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Doomed\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \)  will be
homogeneous with the exception of an interval of 
at most \( \Delta \) cells.

  \item The value of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Doomed\/}}}} \) is true (almost) everywhere 
 if and only if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Hold\/}}}} \) represents the vacant state \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Vac\/}}}^{*} \).

  \item For \( j\in\{-1,1\} \), the value of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \) is equal (almost)
everywhere to \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j}^{*} \) of the cell state represented by the colony.

 \end{cjenum}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The statement~\ref{i:update-loc-maint.damage}
holds by the same reasoning as that of
part~\ref{step:legality.non-free} of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:legality},
because being part of the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \), rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-loc-maint\/}}}} \) 
is also repeated three times.
The effects of later damage on these fields
will be corrected via the rules \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Loc-maintain\/}}}} \);
when damage happens at the end of the work period, its effect is still limited to the location
of the damage rectangle.
The rest of the statement also follows from the error analysis of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \) rule.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:dead-if-long}
  Assume that, for some number \( a \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) does not
intersect \( \{x\}\times(a-T_{\bullet}^{*}/2,a+2T^{\bullet *}] \).
  If \( \eta^{*}(x,\cdot) \) has no switching time during \( (a,a+2T^{\bullet *}] \) then
\( \eta^{*}(x,a+) \) is vacant.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:present-attrib}
 \index{lemma@Lemma!Present Attribution}
 Assume that the live cell \( c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0}) \) in colony \( \mathcal{C}(z_{0}) \)
 is not a germ.                                                               
  Assume also that \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( t_{0} \) does not intersect the healing
wake of any island.
  Then one of the following cases holds.
 \begin{djenum}

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.center}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell, attributed to \( \mathcal{C} \) which is covered by a domain
of member cells at time \( t_{0} \).
If \( {Q}  <\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{0}) <{U} -1-{Q}  \) then every encoded package of this colony
has at most 4 errors.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.new}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell from which a path of time projection at most
  \( {Q} \tau_{2} \) leads back to a growth cell in \( \mathcal{C} \).
  Assume, say, that it is a left growth cell; then it can be attributed to \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \).
  At time \( t_{0} \), if \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \) does not intersect the healing wake of an
island then \( \left[x_{0},z_{0}+2{Q} {B} \right) \) is covered by a multi-domain.
If \( {Q}  <\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{0}) <{U} -1-{Q}  \) then still every encoded package of this colony
has at most 4 errors.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.ext}
    \( c_{0} \) is an outer cell, attributed to its originating colony, say \( \mathcal{C}+ {Q}  {B}  \).
    If \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \) does not intersect the healing wake of an
    island then \( \left[x_{0},z_{0}+2{Q} {B} \right) \) is covered at time \( t_{0} \)
    by a domain.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.vanish}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell, and there is in \( \mathcal{C} \) a backward path from
it, with time projection \( \le 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+({Q} +1)\tau_{2} \),
to a domain of doomed member cells covering \( \mathcal{C} \).

 \end{djenum}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
\begin{step+}{present-attrib.old-member}
Suppose that \( c_{0} \) is a member cell.
  \end{step+}
  \begin{prooof}
    \begin{sloppypar}
      Recall the notation \( K,E_{0} \) from~\eqref{eq:J-K} and
Definition~\ref{def:attrib} (Attribution).
By Lemma~\ref{lem:attrib} (Attribution), \( c_{0} \) can be attributed to the originating
colony \( \mathcal{C} \) which is either the colony of \( c_{0} \) or not.
Let time \( t_{1}\in K\setminus E_{0} \) be a time when \( \mathcal{C} \) was covered by member cells.
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back} (Colony Trace-back),         
we can go back from \( t_{1} \) to a time \( t_{2} \)
before age \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \) in \( \mathcal{C} \).
Then as in part~\ref {step:legality.non-free} of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:legality}
(Legality), we can follow the development of the colony forwards and see that it
forms a continuous domain together with its extension.
The locations containing encoded information have at most
4 errors---as seen in the same proof.      
    \end{sloppypar}

If the computation results in a nonvacant value for the represented big
cell then, if \( \mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}(z_{0}) \) then case~\ref{i:present-attrib.center} holds.
The condition \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}>{Q} \) guarantees that all cells of the colony belong to the same
work period.
Otherwise the represented field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j} \) of the colony will be broadcast
into the field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \) of its cells, as shown in 
Lemma~\ref{lem:update-loc-maint}.
The homogeneity of this latter field will be maintained by the healing rule and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Loc-maintain\/}}}} \).
Thus, depending on the value of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j} \) of the big cell, growth
will take place and the growth forms a continuous domain with the
originating colony until the age \( {U} \) when growth cells turn into members,
and we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.new}.
By the property of the growth rule
the colony encodes a latent big cell, so the statement about errors also holds.

Suppose that the computation results in a vacant value.
Then \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \) will be 0 everywhere but in the healable wake of
the damage.
Growth cannot start accidentally by a temporary wrong value
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j}=1 \) in an endcell since there is enough time to correct
this value during the long waiting time of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}} \).          
Also, all cells become doomed.
After \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}=1 \), any doomed cell dies, and
the whole colony decays within \( {Q} \tau_{2} \) time units.
Before that, the colony is full.
After that, we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.vanish}.
\end{prooof}                            

  \begin{step+}{present-attrib.outer}
  If \( c_{0} \) is an outer cell then we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.ext}.
  \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
  Lemma~\ref{lem:attrib} (Attribution) attributes \( c_{0} \) to the originating colony which is
  covered by member cells during \( K\setminus E_{0} \).
  If \( c_{0} \) is a channel cell then this colony would not have time until \( t_{0} \)
  even to finish its computation, so it could not be destroyed.
  If \( c_{0} \) is a growth cell then the
  cell represented by this colony could not have become vacant, because
  then \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}^{*}_{j} \) would have become 0, broadcast as \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}=0 \) and so
  no growth would have occurred.
  
  It forms a continuous domain with its extension, until the age \( {U} -1 \).              
  From that age on, they form a multi-domain.
  This could only change if the originating colony goes through a next work
  period and kills itself; however, there is not enough time for this:
  the definitions~\eqref{eq:destr-time}, \eqref{eq:compute-start} show that
  \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q} \) is much smaller than \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \).
 \end{pproof}
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:retr.trans}                              
  For a trajectory \( \eta \),
  Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.trans} holds for the decoded trajectory \( \eta^{*} \).

<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
et us take times \( v_{2}, v_{1} \) close from below \( \sigma_{2},\sigma_{1} \)
as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:legality} (Legality).
From time \( v_{1} \) on, follow the development of colony \( \mathcal{C} \).
The computation process can be treated similarly to the proof in 
that lemma; but in the communication with neighbor colonies, we must show that all retrieved
information can be attributed to a single time.
By event~\eqref{eq:no-big-damage}, the whole space-time area in
which this communication takes place contains at most one damage rectangle.
Repeated application of Lemma~\ref{lem:creation} (Creation) guarantees the success of
extending arms via the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Extend\/}}}} \), defined in Section~\ref{sec:growth},
over possible latent or germ cells or an opposing extension arm,
showing that in each direction, within a good time bound either the extension arm of the
colony \( \mathcal{C} \)
reaches its neighbor \( \mathcal{C}' \) (provided it exists) or the neighbor's  reaches it.
If there are extension arms from both colony \( \mathcal{C} \) and a non-adjacent
neighbor colony \( \mathcal{C}' \) then the strength ordering gives preference to one
side and therefore soon only (at most) one arm remains on each side.

\begin{sloppypar}
  In what follows, we call the space-time points \emph{free} if they are outside
  the wake of the damage rectangle (see~\eqref{eq:wake}).
Cell \( x \) is called free at time \( t \) and time \( t \) is called free at cell \( x \)  if \( (x,t) \) is free.
We must find a time during
the communication period \( (0,\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}}] \) of \( \mathcal{C} \) introduced in
Definition~\ref{def:expansion-period} to which the retrieval from both neighbors
can be attributed.
Let \( a_{1} \) be the last free time when some cell of \( \mathcal{C} \)
has age \( 0 \), and \( b_{1} \) the first free time when some such cell
has age \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \), and let \(  J_{1}=(a_{1},b_{1}] \).
By~\eqref{eq:safe-part} and the argument after it, we have 
\begin{align*}
 |J_{1}|>1.5KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}},
\end{align*}
while the unsafe parts of the work period (the dwell period of the big cell simulated by \( \mathcal{C} \))
have a total length \( < 1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \).
Retrieval by rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \) in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Retrieve-2} happens
in points of \( J_{1} \) (provided it did not happen earlier) if
a safe \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \)  as defined in~\eqref{eq:Safe} has been seen in both neighbors.
We will find a sufficiently large subinterval of \( J_{1}\) when this condition holds.
Let \( m_{1} \) be the midpoint of \( J_{1} \).
\end{sloppypar}

\begin{step+}{retr.middle-live}
  Suppose that at time \( m_{1} \) the big cell \( x \) encoded by colony \( \mathcal{C} \) has a left neighbor big cell,
  encoded by a colony \( \mathcal{C}' \).
  Then there is a time interval \( J_{2}\subseteq J_{1} \)
  of size \(  \ge 0.7KR{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \)
  is safe. 
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:present-attrib} that \( m_{1} \) is contained in a dwell period \( D \)
  of the big cell encoded by \( \mathcal{C}' \), of length \( \geT_{\bullet}^{*} \).
  By~\eqref{eq:safe-part}, \( D \) has a subinterval \( J' \)
  of size at least \(  1.5KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) is safe.
  Without loss of generality assume that \( J' \) is above \( m_{1} \).
  In the worst case all the unsafe parts of \( D \) may come above \( m_{1} \): still,
  the  part \( J_{2} \) of \( J' \) falling into \( J_{1} \) has a length of at least
  \begin{align*}
   |J_{1}|/2-1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \ge 0.7KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}}
  \end{align*}
  if \( K \) is large enough.  
\end{pproof}

\begin{step+}{retr.middle-dead}
  Suppose that at time \( m_{1} \) the big cell \( x \) encoded by colony \( \mathcal{C} \) has no left neighbor big cell.
  Then there is a time interval \( J_{2}\subseteq J_{1} \)  of size
  \(  \ge 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) is safe. 
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Let \( J' \) be the largest subinterval of \( J_{1}\) containing \( m_{1} \) in which \( \mathcal{C} \) has no left neighbor.
  Then either \( |J'|>|J_{1}|/3 \) or there is a subinterval of \( J_{1} \) of size \( \ge |J_{1}|/3 \) that
  either contains a whole work period of a left neighbor of \( \mathcal{C} \) or is covered by it.
  In each case, similarly to the reasoning in part~\ref{retr.middle-live} above,
  a safe time subinterval \( J_{2} \) is found of size at least 
  \begin{align*}
   |J_{1}|/3-1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \ge 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}}
  \end{align*}
  if \( K  \) is large enough.
\end{pproof}

We found a time interval \( J_{2} \) of size \( 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \)
in which both \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) are safe.
Repeating the argument we find a time interval \( J_{3}\subset J_{2} \)
of size \( 0.1KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which also \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{1} \) is safe.
  This shows that the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \) rule will succeed at some time \( t' \)
  during the work period of \( \mathcal{C} \) and the simulation result can be attributed to this time point \( t' \) just
  as Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.trans} requires.
<!-- end proof-42 -->

  holds for the decoded trajectory \( \eta^{*} \).
